summary: Bhatt, Morrow and Scholze construct, for a proper smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C, a perfect A_inf-complex RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) = RΓ(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛) with AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μRν_*A_inf,X, whose cohomology groups are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and which specializes to crystalline cohomology of the special fibre, de Rham cohomology, crystalline cohomology over A_crys and étale cohomology of the generic fibre (Theorems 1.8, 1.10). The décalage Lη turns Faltings' almost purity into honest quasi-isomorphisms; locally AΩ is a q-de Rham complex (Theorem 1.17), and its Witt-vector specializations are the relative de Rham–Witt complexes of Langer–Zink (§11). Consequences: for proper smooth formal O_K-schemes the torsion in H^i_crys bounds that in H^i_et, and if H^i_crys and H^{i+1}_crys are torsion-free, H^i_crys is recovered from the Galois lattice via Kisin's modules (Theorem 1.1); over C one recovers it via Fargues' classification and a new B_dR^+-cohomology of proper smooth rigid spaces, which also gives degeneration of the Hodge–Tate spectral sequence (Theorem 1.7). §2 gives two surfaces showing the torsion inequality is sharp and not a subquotient relation. The atlas already plans this material: AInfCohomology AI.0–AI.5 and AI.7 are built on BMS1 (§§3–4, 6–12, 14), CohomologyComparisons CP.2, CP.3 and CP.5 on Theorems 1.1, 1.7 and §§13–14, and CrystallineCohomology CR.4 on its use of Langer–Zink. So BMS1 becomes a source of those layers: its main results are planned, and its supporting lemmas are routed to the layers that use them, with small inputs to PerfectoidQuotients Q0, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4, CrystallineCohomology CR.3 and PadicHodgeTheory P8. No Part II or new roadmap is needed. Eighteen misprints are recorded, all present in the published version; no error or gap was found.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(i): crystalline comparison for proper smooth formal O_K-schemes
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k and ring of integers O_K, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O_K, let C be a completed algebraic closure of K and 𝔛_C the geometric rigid-analytic generic fibre, and fix i ≥ 0. There is a comparison isomorphism H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys, compatible with the G_K-actions, the Frobenius and the filtrations (after extending scalars to B_dR). In particular H^i_et(𝔛_C, Q_p) is a crystalline G_K-representation.
items.note: CP.2 names BMS1 Theorem 1.1(i) and §§12–14 as its source. The proof combines Theorem 14.5(i) (item 006), the Berthelot–Ogus-type Proposition 13.21 (item 189) and the compatibility of Theorem 13.1 with Scholze's de Rham comparison (item 018).

items.name: Theorem 1.1(ii): crystalline torsion bounds étale torsion
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.1, for all n ≥ 0, length_{W(k)}(H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k))_tor/p^n) ≥ length_{Z_p}(H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p)_tor/p^n). In particular, if H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is p-torsion-free then so is H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p).
items.note: CP.5 states this inequality from AI.5's BKF linear algebra (Corollary 4.15, item 070). The converse implication is false (Theorem 2.1, item 023).

items.name: The mod p de Rham bound for étale cohomology
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.1, dim_k H^i_dR(𝔛_k) ≥ dim_{F_p} H^i_et(𝔛_C, F_p) for every i.
items.note: Follows from Theorem 1.1(ii) in degrees i and i+1 and the universal coefficient sequences for H^*_crys ⊗^L k = H^*_dR(𝔛_k) and H^*_et(−, Z_p) ⊗^L F_p. CP.5: 'Prove the mod-p de Rham dimension bound'. Theorem 2.10 and Remark 2.11 show it can be strict.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(iii): recovering crystalline cohomology from étale cohomology
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.1 assume that H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) and H^{i+1}_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) are p-torsion-free. Then H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p) is a lattice in a crystalline G_K-representation, and Kisin's finite free Breuil–Kisin module BK(H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p)) over 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] (Theorem 4.4) satisfies BK(H^i_et(𝔛_C, Z_p)) ⊗_𝔖 W(k) = H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) as φ-stable submodules of their common base extension to W(k)[1/p], where 𝔖 → W(k) sends T to 0 and is the Frobenius on W(k). The identification of base extensions comes from BK ⊗_𝔖 B_crys^+ ≅ H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys^+ (Proposition 4.34 and part (i)).
items.locator: Theorem 1.1(iii) and the paragraph after Remark 1.3, pp. 221–223; Theorem 14.6(iii), p. 394
items.note: CP.5 keeps the torsion-freeness hypotheses in degrees i and i+1 and uses 'the actual Kisin/BKF comparison' (Proposition 4.34, item 061). The proof is Theorem 14.5(iii) (item 008) plus Proposition 4.34.

items.name: Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2 have nonzero H^1_dR
items.statement: Let S_k be an Enriques surface over a perfect field k of characteristic 2 which lifts to a proper smooth scheme over the ring of integers of a complete discretely valued extension of W(k)[1/p] (every Enriques surface does, by Ekedahl and Liedtke). Then H^1_dR(S_k/k) ≠ 0.
items.note: Proof: the geometric generic fibre S_C is an Enriques surface with π_1 = Z/2, so H^1_et(S_C, F_2) ≅ F_2, and inequality (1) (item 003) forces H^1_dR(S_k) ≠ 0. Illusie had observed this by classification ([Illusie 1979, Corollaire 7.3.4(a)]). The lifting theorem is a cited input (Liedtke 2015).

items.name: Theorem 14.5(i): crystalline comparison over O_C and the B_dR^+-lattice
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, 𝔛 a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and i ≥ 0. There is a canonical isomorphism H^i_crys(𝔛_{O/p}/A_crys) ⊗_{A_crys} B_crys ≅ H^i_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys, compatible with the isomorphism H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊗_{B_dR^+} B_dR ≅ H^i_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR of Theorem 13.1 via the identification H^i_crys(𝔛_{O/p}/A_crys) ⊗_{A_crys} B_dR^+ ≅ H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+).
items.note: Proof: Theorem 14.1(iii) and (iv) (items 016, 017); the compatibility is checked on the explicit complexes of §§12–13. CP.2 builds the chain of maps to B_cris, and CP.3 the compatibility with the B_dR^+ deformation.

items.name: Theorem 14.5(ii): the torsion inequality over O_C
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 14.5, for all n ≥ 0, length_{W(k)}(H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k))_tor/p^n) ≥ length_{Z_p}(H^i_et(X, Z_p)_tor/p^n); in particular H^i_et(X, Z_p) is p-torsion-free if H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is.
items.note: Proof: Theorem 14.1, Lemma 4.16 and Corollary 4.15 applied to H^i_{A_inf}(𝔛), with the elementary fact that for an injection M ↪ N of finitely generated W(k)-modules with torsion cokernel Q, length(N/p^n) ≥ length(M/p^n), since length Tor_1(Q, W(k)/p^n) = length(Q/p^n).

items.name: Theorem 1.4 / 14.5(iii): recovering crystalline cohomology over O_C via Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 14.5 assume that H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is p-torsion-free. Then T = H^i_et(X, Z_p) is finite free, Ξ = H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊂ T ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR is a B_dR^+-lattice, and for the finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module BKF(T) attached to (T, Ξ) by Fargues' theorem there is a canonical φ-equivariant isomorphism H^i_{A_inf}(𝔛) ≅ BKF(T) and an inclusion H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) ⊇ BKF(T) ⊗_{A_inf} W(k), compatible with φ. If H^{i+1}_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is also p-torsion-free the inclusion is an equality; so H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) with its φ is recovered functorially from X.
items.note: Proof: Theorem 4.28 (item 081) with Corollary 4.20 (item 075) and part (i). CP.5 owns the lattice-recovery application and AI.5 the BKF properties of H^i_{A_inf}.

items.name: Theorem 1.8 / 14.3: A_inf-cohomology is a perfect complex with Breuil–Kisin–Fargues cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and put RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) := RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛). Then RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) is a perfect complex of A_inf-modules, equipped with a φ-linear map φ : RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) → RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) inducing a quasi-isomorphism RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛)[1/ξ] ≃ RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛)[1/φ(ξ)], and every H^i_{A_inf}(𝔛) is a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module.
items.note: AI.5: 'construct RΓ_Ainf = RΓ(𝔛, AΩ). Prove perfectness and finite presentation of its cohomology, and that the latter satisfy the BKF conditions.' Proof: AΩ_R is derived ξ-complete (Lemma 6.19), so perfectness reduces to the de Rham specialization; the Frobenius is Proposition 9.17; finite freeness after inverting p is Corollary 4.20 with the A_crys and étale comparisons and Proposition 13.21.

items.name: Theorem 1.8(i) / 14.3(i): the crystalline specialization of A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and put RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) := RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛). Then RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗^L_{A_inf} W(k) ≃ RΓ_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)).
items.note: Global form of Theorem 14.1(i) (item 014). CP.1 lists it as the 'derived Witt reduction' row.

items.name: Theorem 1.8(ii) / 14.3(ii): the de Rham specialization of A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and put RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) := RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛). Then RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ} O ≃ RΓ_dR(𝔛/O), the de Rham cohomology of the p-adic formal scheme 𝔛.

items.name: Theorem 1.8(iii) / 14.3(iii): the A_crys specialization of A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and put RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) := RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛). Then RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_crys ≃ RΓ_crys(𝔛_{O/p}/A_crys), where A_crys is the universal p-adically complete PD thickening of O/p compatible with the divided powers of p.

items.name: Theorem 1.8(iv) / 14.3(iv): the étale specialization of A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p with ring of integers O and residue field k, let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X, and put RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) := RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛). Then RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf[1/μ] ≃ RΓ_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/μ], where μ = [ε] − 1 for a compatible system ε of primitive p-power roots of unity.
items.note: Uses Theorem 5.7 (item 092): RΓ_et(X, Z_p) ⊗ A_inf → RΓ(X_proet, A_inf,X) has cone killed by W(𝔪^♭), hence is an isomorphism after inverting μ.

items.name: Theorem 1.10(i) / 14.1(i): AΩ recovers the de Rham–Witt complex of the special fibre
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p (a perfectoid field containing all p-power roots of unity suffices, Remark 14.2) with ring of integers O and residue field k, and let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X. There is a canonical quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves on 𝔛_Zar, compatible with multiplicative structures, AΩ_𝔛 ⊗̂^L_{A_inf} W(k) ≃ WΩ^•_{𝔛_k/W(k)} (p-adically completed tensor product; the right side computes crystalline cohomology of 𝔛_k).
items.note: Proved either from part (iii) or via θ_r-specializations: AΩ ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ_r} W_r(O) ≃ (Lη_{ξ̃_r}AΩ) ⊗^L_{θ̃_r} W_r(O) ≃ H^•(AΩ/ξ̃_r) ≅ W_rΩ^{•,cont}_{𝔛/O} (Proposition 6.12 and Theorem 11.1), then base change to W_r(k) and a limit over r. The proof also sketches that the two resulting identifications with W_rΩ^{•,cont} agree.

items.name: Theorem 1.10(ii) / 14.1(ii): AΩ recovers the de Rham complex
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p (a perfectoid field containing all p-power roots of unity suffices, Remark 14.2) with ring of integers O and residue field k, and let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X. There is a canonical quasi-isomorphism AΩ_𝔛 ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ} O ≃ Ω^{•,cont}_{𝔛/O}, where Ω^{i,cont}_{𝔛/O} = lim_n Ω^i_{(𝔛/p^n)/(O/p^n)}, compatible with multiplicative structures.
items.note: AI.4: 'the theta specialization, which yields the actual de Rham complex'. Second proof: AΩ ⊗^L_θ O ≅ (Lη_{ξ̃}AΩ) ⊗^L_{θ̃} O ≅ H^•(AΩ/ξ̃) ≅ Ω^{•,cont} by Proposition 6.12 and Theorem 8.3.

items.name: Theorem 1.10(iii) / 12.1 / 14.1(iii): the A_crys comparison
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p (a perfectoid field containing all p-power roots of unity suffices, Remark 14.2) with ring of integers O and residue field k, and let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X. Let Y = 𝔛 ×_{Spf O} Spec O/p and u : (Y/A_crys)_crys → 𝔛_Zar the projection. There is a canonical isomorphism AΩ_𝔛 ⊗̂^L_{A_inf} A_crys ≃ Ru_* O^crys_{Y/A_crys} in D(𝔛_Zar); if 𝔛 is qcqs this gives RΓ(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛) ⊗̂^L_{A_inf} A_crys ≃ RΓ_crys(Y/A_crys). The isomorphism can be made one of E_∞-A_crys-algebras.
items.locator: Theorem 1.10(iii), p. 227; Theorem 12.1, p. 357; §12.3, p. 367; Theorem 14.1(iii), p. 388
items.note: AI.4: 'Build the absolute A_cris comparison by compatible PD envelopes and the all-coordinates construction'. The proof is §12 (items 167–175); the E_∞ upgrade of §12.3 assumes an ∞-categorical lift of Lη.

items.name: Theorem 1.10(iv) / 14.1(iv): AΩ recovers nearby cycles of A_inf,X after inverting μ
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p (a perfectoid field containing all p-power roots of unity suffices, Remark 14.2) with ring of integers O and residue field k, and let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over O with generic fibre X. If ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar is the projection, then AΩ_𝔛 ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf[1/μ] ≃ (Rν_* A_inf,X) ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf[1/μ].
items.note: Immediate from the definition AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μ Rν_* A_inf,X, since Lη_μ becomes the identity after inverting μ.

items.name: Theorem 1.7 / 13.1: the B_dR^+-cohomology of proper smooth rigid spaces and its étale comparison
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete extension of Q_p and X a proper smooth adic space over C. Then there are cohomology groups H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+), with RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊗^L_{B_dR^+} C ≃ RΓ_dR(X), which come with a canonical isomorphism H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊗_{B_dR^+} B_dR ≅ H^i_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR. If X = X_0 ⊗̂_K C for a proper smooth rigid space X_0 over a complete discretely valued extension K of Q_p with perfect residue field, this isomorphism agrees with Scholze's comparison H^i_dR(X_0) ⊗_K B_dR ≅ H^i_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR under the identification H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) = H^i_dR(X_0) ⊗_K B_dR^+ (Remark 13.20).
items.locator: Theorem 1.7, p. 224; Theorem 13.1, p. 368; proof, pp. 385–386
items.note: CP.3 constructs this deformation 'by the infinitesimal/PD-style embedding system of BMS1 §13' and proves the comparison after B_dR-inversion; the local comparison is Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+} ≃ η_ξ K_{B_dR^+(R_∞,Σ)}((γ_u − 1)_u), proved like Proposition 12.9.

items.name: Theorem 13.19: B_dR^+-cohomology is finite free
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth adic space over an algebraically closed complete extension C of Q_p. Then H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) is a finite free B_dR^+-module for every i ∈ Z.
items.note: Proof: realize X as the fibre at η ∈ S(C) of a proper smooth family f : 𝒳 → S = Spa(A, A°) over K = W(k)[1/p] (Corollary 13.16, item 187), lift A → C to A → B_dR^+ by smoothness, and compare Rf_{dR*}O_𝒳 ⊗^L_A B_dR^+ with RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+) modulo ξ; the R^i f_{dR*} are locally free, having integrable connections. CP.3: 'Prove finite freeness in the source scope'.

items.name: Theorem 1.7(i) / 13.3(i): degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence (Conrad–Gabber)
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth adic space over an algebraically closed complete extension C of Q_p. The Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence E_1^{ij} = H^j(X, Ω^i_{X/C}) ⇒ H^{i+j}_dR(X) degenerates at E_1.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7(i), p. 224; Theorem 13.3(i), p. 369; proof, p. 386
items.note: Proof: spread X out over a smooth base S over a discretely valued field (Corollary 13.16) so that all R^i f_*Ω^j and R^i f_{dR*} are locally free and commute with base change, and check the rank equality at classical points, where it is Scholze's [Corollary 1.8]. CP.3: 'Prove filtration strictness and the Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons in characteristic zero'.

items.name: Theorem 1.7(ii) / 13.3(ii): degeneration of the Hodge–Tate spectral sequence
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth adic space over an algebraically closed complete extension C of Q_p. The Hodge–Tate spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^i(X, Ω^j_{X/C})(−j) ⇒ H^{i+j}_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} C degenerates at E_2.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7(ii), p. 224; Theorem 13.3(ii), p. 369; proof, p. 386
items.note: Proof: dim H^i_dR(X) = Σ_j dim H^{i−j}(X, Ω^j) by part (i); dim H^i_dR(X) = rank H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) (Theorem 13.19) = rank H^i_et(X, Z_p) ⊗ B_dR^+ (Theorem 13.1); so the E_2 page already has the dimension of the abutment.

items.name: Torsion-freeness of H^i_crys is equivalent to torsion-freeness of H^i_dR
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O_C (or over O_K as in Theorem 1.1) and fix i. Then H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is torsion-free if and only if H^i_dR(𝔛) is torsion-free. Consequently every torsion-freeness hypothesis on H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) in Theorems 1.1(ii),(iii) and 14.5(ii),(iii) may be replaced by the same hypothesis on the O-module H^i_dR(𝔛).
items.locator: Footnote to Theorem 1.1(ii), p. 221; Remark 4.21, p. 276; Remark 14.4, p. 392; Remark 14.7, p. 395
items.note: Proof: Theorem 14.3(i),(ii) and Lemma 4.18 (item 073) applied to C = RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛). The authors know no direct crystalline proof for a single index i; the weaker statement for i and i+1 together follows from universal coefficients.

items.name: Theorem 2.1: a smooth projective surface over Z_2 with torsion-free étale but torsion crystalline cohomology
items.statement: There is a smooth projective geometrically connected relative surface X over Z_2 such that H^i_et(X_{Q̄_2}, Z_2) is free over Z_2 for all i ∈ Z, while H^2_crys(X_{F_2}/Z_2)_tor = F_2. So the implication in Theorem 1.1(ii) cannot be reversed. Moreover the cospecialization map H^2_et(X_{F̄_2}, Z_2) → H^2_et(X_{Q̄_2}, Z_2) is not injective (Remark 2.3).
items.locator: Theorem 2.1, p. 236; proof and Remark 2.3, pp. 237–238
items.note: AI.5 and CP.5 use 'the examples of BMS1 §2', and CR.3's acceptance includes 'a torsion cohomology example from BMS1 §2'. Proof: X is a smooth sufficiently ample hypersurface in the 3-fold D of Proposition 2.2 (item 024), chosen over Z_2 by the Bertini theorems of Gabber and Poonen; H^2_et(X_C) is free by the Lefschetz sequence with Artin vanishing for the affine complement, and H^i_crys(D_k) → H^i_crys(X_k) is an isomorphism for i ≤ 1 and injective with torsion-free cokernel for i = 2 by Lemma 2.12 (item 030).

items.name: Proposition 2.2: the 3-fold D over Z_2
items.statement: Let S be a singular Enriques surface over Z_2 (Pic^τ(S) ≅ μ_2; one exists: S̃_{F_2} ⊂ P^5_{F_2} cut out by x_1^2 + x_2x_3 + y_1^2 + x_1y_1 = x_2^2 + x_1x_3 + y_2^2 + x_2y_2 = x_3^2 + x_1x_2 + y_3^2 + x_3y_3 = 0 is a K3 surface with the free involution (x_i : y_i) ↦ (x_i : x_i + y_i), S_{F_2} = S̃_{F_2}/(Z/2) lifts to Z_2 by Lang's theorem, with its K3 double cover S̃ → S). Let E be an ordinary elliptic curve over Z_2, η : Z/2 → μ_2 ⊂ E the map through the canonical subgroup (nonzero over Q_2, zero over F_2), and D → S the E-torsor obtained by pushing out S̃ → S along η. Then D is a smooth projective geometrically connected 3-fold over Z_2, H^i_et(D_{Q̄_2}, Z_2) is free for i = 0, 1, 2, and H^2_crys(D_{F_2}/Z_2)_tor = F_2.
items.note: Proof: D_{F_2} = S_{F_2} × E_{F_2}, so (ii) follows from Künneth and Illusie's computation of H^*_crys of Enriques surfaces [Illusie 1979, Proposition 7.3.5]; for (i), π_1(D_C) ≅ π_1(E'_C) ≅ Ẑ² with E' = E/η, so H_1(D_C, Z_2) is free and H^2 is torsion-free by the universal coefficient sequence. The smoothness of S̃_{F_2} is checked by the Jacobian criterion (footnote 2).

items.name: A_inf-cohomology is not a functor of the special fibre
items.statement: The torsion in the étale cohomology of the generic fibre of a smooth proper Z_2-scheme is not a functor of its special fibre: D (Proposition 2.2) and D' = S × E are two lifts of S_{F_2} × E_{F_2} to Z_2 with H^2_et(D_{Q̄_2}, Z_2) torsion-free and H^2_et(D'_{Q̄_2}, Z_2) containing 2-torsion. Hence RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) (and even RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛)/p) is not a functor of 𝔛_{O/p}.
items.note: Used in Remark 1.9 to explain why the Frobenius on RΓ_{A_inf} does not come from a Frobenius on the special fibre.

items.name: Lemma 2.5: a finite flat group scheme degenerating Z/p^2 to E_k[p]
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a complete algebraically closed extension C of Q_p with residue field k, E/O an elliptic curve with supersingular reduction, x ∈ E(C) a point of exact order p^2, and G ⊂ E the flat closure of the subgroup generated by x. Then G_C ≅ Z/p^2 and G_k = E_k[p].
items.note: Proof: E_k has a unique subgroup scheme of order p^r, the kernel of the r-fold Frobenius. Remark 2.6 explains the heuristic that BG would be a stacky example.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: a projective space with a G-action free outside high codimension
items.statement: Let G be a finite flat group scheme over O (e.g. that of Lemma 2.5). For every integer c there is a projective space P/O with an action of G such that the locus Z_P ⊂ P of points with non-trivial stabilizers — the support of b_*O_F/O_P for b : F → P the base change of the action map G × P → P × P, (g, x) ↦ (gx, x), along the diagonal — has codimension ≥ c on the special fibre. Formation of Z_P commutes with passage to fibres over Spec O and Z_P is G-stable.
items.locator: Lemma 2.7, Remark 2.8 and the following paragraph, pp. 239–240
items.note: Proof: take P = P(V^c) for a faithful representation V with G acting faithfully on each fibre of P(V); Z_P lies in the image of ∏_{i=1}^c Ỹ, which has codimension ≥ c.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: the quotient P/G approximates BG
items.statement: Let h : P → X = P/G be the scheme-theoretic quotient for P and G as in Lemma 2.7 (with c > 2), U_X = U_P/G and Z_X = X ∖ U_X. Then X is projective and flat over O, Z_X has codimension > 2 on the special fibre, and X → Spec O is smooth over U_X.
items.note: Proof: h(Z_P) = Z_X; U_P → U_X is a G-torsor, hence faithfully flat, and U_{X,k} is regular because it receives a faithfully flat map from the regular scheme U_{P,k}.

items.name: Theorem 2.10: torsion Z/p^2 in étale cohomology degenerating to k ⊕ k in crystalline cohomology
items.statement: For O, E and G as in Lemma 2.5, with P and X = P/G as in Lemmas 2.7 and 2.9, let H ⊂ U_X be a smooth complete intersection of dim(P) − 2 hypersurfaces of sufficiently large degree (which exists by Bertini, since Z_X has codimension > 2 on the special fibre). Then H is a smooth projective relative surface over O with H^2_et(H_C, Z_p)_tor ≅ Z/p^2 and H^2_crys(H_k/W(k))_tor ≅ k ⊕ k, and H^1_crys(H_k/W(k)) = 0. So the inequality of Theorem 1.1(ii) cannot be upgraded to a subquotient relation.
items.note: CP.5: 'Do not infer a subquotient relation from the length inequality: BMS1 §2 explicitly supplies counterexamples.' Proof: Leray for the Z/p^2-cover H̃_C → H_C; for crystalline cohomology, the E-torsor H_E → H inside X_E = (P × E)/G, weak Lefschetz (Lemma 2.12) with i_L = 1, and the map E_k → E_k/E_k[p] ≅ E_k inducing multiplication by p on H^1_crys. Remark 2.11 states without proof that H^1_et(H_C, Z/p) ≅ Z/p while H^1_dR(H_k) ≅ k ⊕ k, so inequality (1) can be strict.

items.name: Lemma 2.12: weak Lefschetz for crystalline cohomology with a weakly ample line bundle
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, X a smooth projective variety of dimension d over k and L a line bundle on X, and let i_L ≥ 0 be such that for every coherent sheaf F on X, H^i(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗n}) = 0 for n sufficiently large and i > i_L. Then there is n_0 such that for all n ≥ n_0 and every smooth hypersurface H ⊂ X with divisor L^{⊗n}, the map H^j_crys(X/W(k)) → H^j_crys(H/W(k)) is an isomorphism for j < d − i_L − 1 and injective with torsion-free cokernel for j = d − i_L − 1.
items.note: Berthelot proved the ample case i_L = 0 (C. R. Acad. Sci. 277, 1973); BMS1 give the full argument: reduce the cone modulo p to de Rham cohomology and bound RΓ(X, I^{⊗r} ⊗ Ω^{j−1}_H) by Serre duality and induction on j.

items.name: Fontaine's ring A_inf(S) of a p-adically complete ring
items.statement: Let S be a ring which is π-adically complete and separated for some π ∈ S dividing p, and S^♭ = lim_φ S/pS its tilt. Fontaine's ring is A_inf(S) = W(S^♭), with the Frobenius automorphism φ induced by that of the perfect ring S^♭.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean defines PreTilt O p = Perfection (ModP O p) p, the inverse limit of O/p along Frobenius, and Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean the p-typical Witt vectors; A_inf(S) is WittVector p (PreTilt S p). There is no named declaration for A_inf itself.

items.name: Fontaine's map θ : A_inf(S) → S
items.statement: Let S be a ring which is π-adically complete and separated for some π ∈ S dividing p, and S^♭ = lim_φ S/pS its tilt. There is a ring homomorphism θ : A_inf(S) → S with θ([x]) = x^♯ = x^{(0)} for x = (x^{(0)}, x^{(1)}, …) ∈ S^♭ ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} S; if the Frobenius of S/p is surjective, θ is surjective.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3 (r = 1) and the paragraph after it, p. 246; Lemma 3.9(v), p. 248
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165 defines fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R for any ring, as the limit of maps to R/p^{n+1}; fontaineTheta_teichmuller gives θ([x]) = x.untilt, and surjective_fontaineTheta assumes p is not a unit, R is p-adically complete and Frobenius is surjective on R/p. BMS1's θ is θ_1 of the next items.

items.name: Lemma 3.2: A_inf(S) as an inverse limit of Witt vectors along F
items.statement: Let S be a ring which is π-adically complete and separated for some π ∈ S dividing p, and S^♭ = lim_φ S/pS its tilt. (i) The canonical maps lim_{x ↦ x^p} S → S^♭ → lim_φ S/πS are isomorphisms of monoids/rings. (ii) For f ∈ S, W_r(f^{p^{r−1}}S) ⊂ [f]W_r(S) ⊂ W_r(fS); [p]^2 ∈ pW_r(S) and p^r W_r(S) ⊂ W_r(pS); hence W_r(S) and W(S) are complete for the [π]-, [p]- and p-adic topologies. (iii) φ^∞ : lim_F W_r(S^♭) → lim_R W_r(S^♭) is an isomorphism. (iv) lim_F W_r(S^♭) → lim_F W_r(S/πS) is an isomorphism. (v) lim_F W_r(S) → lim_F W_r(S/πS) is an isomorphism. In particular A_inf(S) ≅ lim_F W_r(S), and under this identification the restriction R corresponds to φ^{−1}, so R is an automorphism of lim_F W_r(S).
items.note: Part (v) uses a pro-isomorphism {W_r(S/π^sS)}_F → {W_r(S/πS)}_F. Part (i) for Mathlib's PreTilt is the multiplicative map PreTilt.untilt; parts (ii)–(v) are not in the libraries.

items.name: The maps θ_r, θ̃_r : A_inf(S) → W_r(S) and θ_∞
items.statement: Let S be a ring which is π-adically complete and separated for some π ∈ S dividing p, and S^♭ = lim_φ S/pS its tilt. Through A_inf(S) = lim_R W_r(S^♭) ← lim_F W_r(S^♭) → lim_F W_r(S/πS) ← lim_F W_r(S) (Lemma 3.2), the projections define θ̃_r : A_inf(S) → W_r(S), and θ_r := θ̃_r ∘ φ^r. For x ∈ S^♭, θ_r([x]) = [x^{(0)}] and θ̃_r([x]) = [x^{(r)}] (Lemma 3.3); θ = θ_1 is Fontaine's map, and θ_r composed with W_r(S) → W_r(S/pS) equals the restriction of A_inf(S) → W_r(S^♭) followed by W_r of S^♭ → S/pS. Letting r → ∞ gives θ_∞ : A_inf(S) → W(S) with θ_∞([x]) = [x^{(0)}].
items.locator: §3.1, construction before Lemma 3.3, Lemma 3.3 and the paragraphs after it, pp. 246–247
items.note: AI.0 plans θ and θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{−1}; the Witt-level maps θ_r, θ̃_r for all r, which drive §§9–11, are not named.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: θ_r and θ̃_r intertwine R, F and V
items.statement: Let S be a ring which is π-adically complete and separated for some π ∈ S dividing p, and S^♭ = lim_φ S/pS its tilt. Then θ_r = R ∘ θ_{r+1}, F ∘ θ_{r+1} = θ_r ∘ φ, and V ∘ θ_r = θ_{r+1}(λ_{r+1}·φ^{−1}(−)) for any λ_{r+1} ∈ A_inf(S) with θ_{r+1}(λ_{r+1}) = V(1). Equivalently R ∘ θ̃_{r+1} = θ̃_r ∘ φ^{−1}, F ∘ θ̃_{r+1} = θ̃_r, and V ∘ θ̃_r = θ̃_{r+1}(λ̃_{r+1}·(−)) with λ̃_{r+1} = φ^{r+1}(λ_{r+1}), θ̃_{r+1}(λ̃_{r+1}) = V(1).

items.name: Perfectoid rings
items.statement: A ring S is perfectoid if it is π-adically complete for some π ∈ S such that π^p divides p, the Frobenius φ : S/pS → S/pS is surjective, and ker(θ : A_inf(S) → S) is principal. Examples: perfect F_p-algebras (π = 0), the p-adic completion Z_p^cycl of Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}] and of the integers of any algebraic extension of Q_p containing it, and Z_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
items.locator: Definition 3.5 and Example 3.6, pp. 247–248; Remarks 3.7–3.8, p. 248
items.note: Q0:integral-algebra constructs integral perfectoid rings in the scope of BS22, whose definition is equivalent. Remark 3.8 shows the definition agrees with Gabber–Ramero's (independently of the topology).

items.name: Lemma 3.9: surjectivity of Frobenius on perfectoid-type rings
items.statement: Let S be π-adically complete for some π with π^p | p. The following are equivalent: (i) every element of S/πpS is a p-th power; (ii) every element of S/pS is a p-th power; (iii) every element of S/π^pS is a p-th power; (iv) F : W_{r+1}(S) → W_r(S) is surjective for all r ≥ 1; (v) θ_r : A_inf(S) → W_r(S) is surjective for all r ≥ 1. If they hold, there are units u, v ∈ S^× such that uπ and vp admit compatible systems of p-power roots in S.
items.note: (ii) ⇒ (iv) uses Davis–Kedlaya, On the Witt vector Frobenius, implication (xiv)' ⇒ (ii).

items.name: Lemma 3.10: kernel of θ principal iff Frobenius is an isomorphism
items.statement: Let S be π-adically complete with π^p | p and φ : S/πS → S/π^pS surjective. (i) If ker θ is principal, then φ : S/πS → S/π^pS is an isomorphism and every generator of ker θ is a non-zero-divisor. (ii) Conversely, if φ : S/πS → S/π^pS is an isomorphism and π is a non-zero-divisor, then ker θ is principal, so S is perfectoid. In the proof, after scaling π by a unit, ξ = p + [π^♭]^p x ∈ ker θ is shown to generate ker θ.
items.note: P1 plans the Tate version ('Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism', principal non-zero-divisor kernel of θ); Q0 the integral version.

items.name: Distinguished elements generate ker θ
items.statement: Let S be perfectoid and ξ = (ξ_0, ξ_1, …) ∈ ker θ. Then ξ generates ker θ if and only if ξ is distinguished, i.e. ξ_1 ∈ (S^♭)^×. Any ξ ∈ A_inf(S) with θ_r(ξ) = V(1) for some r > 1 (which exists by Lemma 3.9(v)) is distinguished; the image of a distinguished element under a map of perfectoid rings is distinguished.
items.locator: Remark 3.11, p. 250; proof of Lemma 3.13, p. 251
items.note: PR.0 constructs distinguished elements and the perfect-prism correspondence that Q0 imports.

items.name: Lemma 3.12: kernels of θ_r and θ̃_r
items.statement: Let S be perfectoid and ξ a generator of ker θ. For every r ≥ 1, ker θ_r is generated by the non-zero-divisor ξ_r = ξφ^{−1}(ξ)⋯φ^{−(r−1)}(ξ), and ker θ̃_r by ξ̃_r = φ^r(ξ_r) = φ(ξ)φ^2(ξ)⋯φ^r(ξ). Hence A_inf(S)/ξ̃_r ≅ W_r(S) via θ̃_r.

items.name: Lemma 3.13: Tor-independence of Witt vectors of perfectoid rings
items.statement: Let S → S' be a map of perfectoid rings and 1 ≤ j ≤ r. Then W_j(S) ⊗^L_{A_inf(S)} A_inf(S') → W_j(S') and W_j(S) ⊗^L_{W_r(S)} W_r(S') → W_j(S') are quasi-isomorphisms, with W_j(S) a W_r(S)-module via either F or R.

items.name: Lemma 3.14: the cotangent complex of a map of perfectoid rings vanishes mod p
items.statement: For a map S → S' of perfectoid rings, L_{S'/S} ⊗^L_Z F_p ≃ 0; in particular the derived p-adic completion L̂_{S'/S} vanishes.
items.note: Proof: S' = S ⊗^L_{A_inf(S)} A_inf(S'), and L_{A_inf(S')/A_inf(S)} ⊗^L F_p ≃ L_{S'^♭/S^♭} ≃ 0 since the cotangent complex of a perfect F_p-algebra vanishes.

items.name: Perfectoid rings of characteristic p are the perfect rings
items.statement: A ring S of characteristic p is perfectoid if and only if it is perfect; then S^♭ = S, θ_∞ : A_inf(S) → W(S) is an isomorphism and the θ_r are the Witt vector restriction maps.
items.note: P1: 'the characteristic-p characterization as perfect complete Tate rings'; Q0 the integral version.

items.name: The element ξ attached to p-power roots of unity
items.statement: Let S be perfectoid with a compatible system ζ_{p^r} of p-power roots of unity with 1 + ζ_p + ⋯ + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0 (this includes the characteristic-p case with all ζ_{p^r} = 1), and ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ S^♭. Then ξ := 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + ⋯ + [ε^{1/p}]^{p−1} generates ker θ and θ_r(ξ) = V(1) for all r > 1, so ker θ̃_r is generated by ξ̃_r = Σ_{i=0}^{p^r−1} [ε]^i.
items.note: AI.0: 'define mu = [epsilon] − 1, xi = mu/phi^(−1)(mu) … Prove the displayed quotient exists and generates the stated ideal'. BMS1 prove it for every perfectoid S with such roots of unity, by reduction to Z_p^cycl and ghost components.

items.name: Proposition 3.17: the element μ
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid ring, flat over Z_p, containing a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, with ε, ξ, ξ̃_r as above and μ = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf(S). For every r ≥ 0: (i) θ̃_r(μ) = [ζ_{p^r}] − 1 is a non-zero-divisor of W_r(S); (ii) μ is a non-zero-divisor of A_inf(S); (iii) μ divides φ^r(μ) = [ε^{p^r}] − 1 and ξ̃_r = φ^r(μ)/μ; (iv) μ divides ξ̃_r − p^r.
items.note: AI.0: 'Prove nonzerodivisor, completeness and torsion properties used later.'

items.name: Corollary 3.18 and Remark 3.19: ideals of W_r(S) cut out by V^j(1) and F^j
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid ring, flat over Z_p, with a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, and 0 ≤ j ≤ r. (i) Ann_{W_r(S)} V^j(1) = ker(F^j : W_r(S) → W_{r−j}(S)) = (([ζ_{p^j}] − 1)/([ζ_{p^r}] − 1)) W_r(S). (ii) The annihilator of ([ζ_{p^j}] − 1)/([ζ_{p^r}] − 1) equals V^j(1)W_r(S) = V^jW_{r−j}(S). (iii) F^j and multiplication by V^j(1) induce isomorphisms F^j_*W_{r−j}(S) ≅ W_r(S)/(([ζ_{p^j}] − 1)/([ζ_{p^r}] − 1)) ≅ Ann_{W_r(S)}(([ζ_{p^j}] − 1)/([ζ_{p^r}] − 1)). For an arbitrary perfectoid S still Ann V^j(1) = ker F^j, V^j(1)W_r(S) = V^jW_{r−j}(S) and W_{r−j}(S) ≅ W_r(S)/Ann V^j(1) ≅ V^jW_{r−j}(S).

items.name: Lemma 3.20: perfectoid Tate rings and their rings of integral elements
items.statement: Let R be a complete Tate ring with a ring of integral elements R^+ ⊂ R. If R is perfectoid in Fontaine's sense (uniform, with a topologically nilpotent unit π such that π^p | p in R° and Frobenius surjective on R°/π^pR°), then R^+ is a perfectoid ring. Conversely, if R^+ is perfectoid and bounded in R, then R is perfectoid in Fontaine's sense. Perfectoid K-algebras (Scholze) and perfectoid Q_p-algebras (Kedlaya–Liu) are exactly the perfectoid Tate K- (resp. Q_p-) algebras in Fontaine's sense.
items.locator: Lemma 3.20 and the remark after it, p. 255
items.note: Q0: 'their relation to Tate perfectoid rings and integral subrings'. The converse uses Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Lemma 5.5.

items.name: Lemma 3.21: inverting π in a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R_0 be a perfectoid ring which is π-adically complete for a non-zero-divisor π with π^p | p. Then R = R_0[1/π] with the π-adic topology on R_0 is a complete Tate ring, perfectoid in Fontaine's sense, and R_0 ⊂ R° with πR° ⊂ R_0 (the cokernel of R_0 → R° is killed by every fractional power of π).

items.name: The period rings A_crys, B_crys^+, B_crys, B_dR^+ and B_dR of a perfectoid field
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, A_inf = A_inf(O), ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ). A_crys is the p-adic completion of the A_inf-subalgebra of A_inf[1/p] generated by the ξ^m/m!, m ≥ 0 — the universal p-adically complete PD thickening of O (equivalently of O/p) compatible with the PD structure on Z_p; B_crys^+ = A_crys[1/p]; B_crys = A_crys[1/μ] = B_crys^+[1/μ] (μ^{p−1} ∈ pA_crys since μ^{p−1} ≡ ξ^p mod p); B_dR^+ is the ξ-adic completion of B_crys^+, a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field K, and B_dR = B_dR^+[1/ξ].
items.note: CR.0 exports the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ as A_cris; R06.1 constructs B_dR^+, B_cris^+ and B_cris from the same objects.

items.name: Lemma 3.23: the kernel of θ_∞ is generated by μ
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity. The kernel of θ_∞ = lim_r θ_r : A_inf → W(O) = lim_R W_r(O) is μA_inf; equivalently ∩_r (μ/φ^{−r}(μ)) A_inf = μA_inf. In particular the ideal (μ) does not depend on the choice of roots of unity. The cokernel of θ_∞ is killed by W(𝔪^♭), and if K is spherically complete, θ_∞ induces A_inf/μ ≅ W(O).
items.note: AI.0: 'Prove change-of-epsilon comparison.' The cokernel is lim^1_r ξ_r A_inf; spherical completeness of K passes to K^♭.

items.name: Proposition 3.24: W_r(O) is coherent
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field K. For every r ≥ 1 the ring W_r(O) is coherent (every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented). By contrast A_inf is in general not coherent (Kedlaya).
items.note: Proof: in characteristic p, W_r(O) is a successive square-zero extension of the perfect valuation ring O; in characteristic 0, ghost components and Lemmas 3.27–3.28 reduce to W_r(O/p^N), which is built by square-zero extensions from W_{r−1}(O/p^N) (Lemma 3.26).

items.name: Lemma 3.25: coherence passes to quotients by finitely generated ideals
items.statement: Let R be a ring and I ⊂ R a finitely generated ideal. (i) An R/I-module is finitely presented over R/I iff it is finitely presented over R. (ii) If R is coherent, so is R/I.

items.name: Lemma 3.26: coherence lifts along square-zero extensions
items.statement: Let S → R be a surjection of rings with square-zero kernel I. If R is coherent and I is a finitely presented R-module, then S is coherent.

items.name: Lemma 3.27: coherence from R[1/f] and R/f under Artin–Rees
items.statement: Let R be a ring and f ∈ R a non-zero-divisor such that (R, f) has the Artin–Rees property (for finitely generated M ⊂ N the f-adic topology of N restricts to that of M). If R[1/f] and R/f are coherent, then R is coherent.

items.name: Lemma 3.28: the Artin–Rees property is invariant under f-isogeny
items.statement: Let g : R → S be an injective ring map and f ∈ R with R and S f-torsion-free, and with cokernel of g killed by a power of f. Then (R, f) has the Artin–Rees property iff (S, f) does.

items.name: Corollary 3.29: finitely presented W_r(O)-modules have no almost zero elements
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field and M a finitely presented W_r(O)-module. Then no non-zero element of M is killed by W_r(𝔪). (W_r(𝔪) is an increasing union of principal ideals generated by non-zero-divisors, Corollary 10.2.)

items.name: Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. A Breuil–Kisin module is a finitely generated 𝔖-module M with an isomorphism φ_M : M ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔖[1/E] ≅ M[1/E]. With this definition they form an abelian tensor category.
items.note: Same classification as the BMS2 extraction (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/001).

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin twist 𝔖{1}
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. For E_r = Eφ(E)⋯φ^{r−1}(E) put (𝔖/E_r){1} := L_{(𝔖/E_r)/𝔖}[−1] ≅ E_r𝔖/E_r^2𝔖, free of rank 1 over 𝔖/E_r. For r > s the obvious map has image p^{r−s}(𝔖/E_s){1}; dividing by p^{r−s} gives (𝔖/E_r){1} ⊗ 𝔖/E_s ≅ (𝔖/E_s){1}, and 𝔖{1} := lim_r (𝔖/E_r){1} is free of rank 1 with a Frobenius φ_{𝔖{1}}(x) = (u/E)φ(x) for an explicit unit u; it is ⊗-invertible, and M{n} := M ⊗ 𝔖{1}^{⊗n}.
items.note: AI.0 constructs Breuil–Kisin twists 'with source orientation' and PR.3 constructs BK twists of a prism (here (𝔖, (E))).

items.name: Proposition 4.3: structure of Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. Every Breuil–Kisin module (M, φ_M) sits in a canonical exact sequence of Breuil–Kisin modules 0 → M_tor → M → M_free → M̄ → 0, where M_tor is the torsion submodule and is killed by a power of p, M_free is finite free over 𝔖, and M̄ is killed by a power of (p, T). In particular M[1/p] ≅ M_free[1/p] is finite free over 𝔖[1/p].
items.note: M_free = H^0 of the vector bundle on the punctured spectrum of the 2-dimensional regular local ring 𝔖; the p-power torsion bound comes from the Frobenius-stability of Fitting ideals and a Newton-polygon argument on their zeros in the open unit disc.

items.name: Theorem 4.4 (Kisin): Breuil–Kisin modules of crystalline lattices
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. Fix π^{1/p^n} ∈ K̄, K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}), C = K̄^, π^♭ ∈ O_C^♭, and 𝔖 → A_inf by T ↦ [π^♭]^p and Frobenius on W(k) (compatible with θ̃). There is a natural fully faithful tensor functor T ↦ M(T) from Z_p-lattices T in crystalline G_K-representations V to finite free Breuil–Kisin modules; M(T) is characterized by a φ- and G_{K_∞}-equivariant identification M(T) ⊗_𝔖 W(C^♭) ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} W(C^♭). The functor is not exact.
items.note: Cited from Kisin (2006) and Kisin (2010, Theorem 1.2.1); uniqueness uses Kisin's Proposition 2.1.12 and the equivalence between étale φ-modules over the p-adic completion of 𝔖[1/T] and Z_p[G_{K_∞}]-modules. PR.7 compares the prismatic F-crystal classification with 'R07's Kisin functor'.

items.name: Proposition 4.34: Kisin modules and Fargues' classification
items.statement: Let T be a Z_p-lattice in a crystalline G_K-representation V and M(T) its Breuil–Kisin module. Then M(T) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf[1/μ] = T ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (G_{K_∞}-equivariantly), and M(T) ⊗_𝔖 B_crys^+ = D_crys(V) ⊗_{W(k)[1/p]} B_crys^+ as submodules of M(T) ⊗_𝔖 B_crys = T ⊗ B_crys = D_crys(V) ⊗ B_crys. Consequently the finite free BKF module M(T) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf corresponds under Fargues' classification to (T, Ξ) with Ξ = D_crys(V) ⊗ B_dR^+ = D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+, and M(T) ⊗_𝔖 W(k)[1/p] = D_crys(V), so M(T) ⊗_𝔖 W(k) is a lattice in D_crys(V).
items.note: Proof: Kisin's construction starts from D_crys(V) ⊗ 𝔖[1/p] on a rigid-analytic open of the generic fibre of Spf 𝔖 [Kisin 2006, §1.2, Lemma 1.2.6]. CP.5 uses 'the actual Kisin/BKF comparison'.

items.name: Lemma 4.6 (Kedlaya): vector bundles on the punctured spectrum of A_inf
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let s be the closed point of Spec A_inf and U = Spec A_inf ∖ {s}. Restriction is an equivalence between vector bundles on Spec A_inf and on U; in particular every vector bundle on U is free.
items.note: U = Spec A_inf[1/p] ∪ Spec A_inf[1/x]; the proof bounds j_*ℰ inside a finitely generated module and uses Lemmas 4.7–4.8 over the valuation ring O^♭ (first explained in Scholze–Weinstein's Berkeley lectures).

items.name: Lemma 4.7: submodules of (K^♭)^d have at most d generators modulo 𝔪
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Every O^♭-submodule E of (K^♭)^d satisfies dim_k(E ⊗ k) ≤ d.

items.name: Lemma 4.8: a freeness criterion over O^♭
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. If D ⊂ (K^♭)^d is an O^♭-submodule with dim_k(D ⊗ k) = d, then D is finite free of rank d.

items.name: Lemma 4.9: finitely presented A_inf-modules free after inverting p are perfect
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A_inf-module with M[1/p] finite free over A_inf[1/p]. (i) M is perfect as an A_inf-complex. (ii) Its torsion submodule M_tor is killed by p^n for n ≫ 0 and is finitely presented and perfect. (iii) M has Tor-dimension ≤ 2 and Tor_2^{A_inf}(M, W(k)) = 0; if M has no x-torsion then Tor_i^{A_inf}(M, W(k)) = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Uses coherence of W_n(O^♭) and the sequence 0 → Q → W̃ → W(k) → 0 with W̃ = colim_n A_inf/(x^{1/p^n}).

items.name: Lemma 4.10: p-torsion-free A_inf-modules give vector bundles on the punctured spectrum
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let M be a finitely generated p-torsion-free A_inf-module with M[1/p] finite projective over A_inf[1/p]. Then the associated quasi-coherent sheaf restricts to a vector bundle on U = Spec A_inf ∖ {s}. (M itself need not be projective, e.g. M = (x, p).)
items.note: A_inf localized at (p) is a discrete valuation ring (valuation: the first nonzero Teichmüller coefficient).

items.name: Corollary 4.12: finite projective A_inf[1/p]-modules are free
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Every finite projective A_inf[1/p]-module is free.

items.name: Proposition 4.13: structure of finitely presented A_inf-modules
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A_inf-module with M[1/p] finite projective (equivalently free) over A_inf[1/p]. There is a functorial exact sequence 0 → M_tor → M → M_free → M̄ → 0 with M_tor finitely presented, perfect and killed by p^n for n ≫ 0; M_free finite free; and M̄ finitely presented, perfect and killed by a power of (x, p). Moreover M is finite free if M ⊗_{A_inf} W(k) is p-torsion-free, or if K has characteristic 0 and M ⊗_{A_inf} O is p-torsion-free.
items.note: AI.2: 'torsion decompositions and the étale/Witt specializations'.

items.name: Lemma 4.14: lengths go up under specialization
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let M be a finitely presented W_n(O^♭)-module, M_η = M ⊗ W_n(K^♭) and M_s = M ⊗ W_n(k). Then M_η and M_s have finite length and ℓ(M_η) = ℓ(M_s) − ℓ(Tor_1^{W_n(O^♭)}(M, W_n(k))) ≤ ℓ(M_s).

items.name: Corollary 4.15: elementary divisors under specialization
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A_inf-module with M[1/p] free over A_inf[1/p], M_1 = M ⊗ W(K^♭) and M_2 = M ⊗ W(k). Then M_1 and M_2 have the same rank, and ℓ(M_2/p^n) ≥ ℓ(M_1/p^n) for all n ≥ 1.
items.note: AI.5: 'Prove the linear algebra controlling integral torsion under these specializations'; the length estimate is the input to Theorems 1.1(ii) and 14.5(ii).

items.name: Lemma 4.16: the crystalline specialization map on cohomology is injective
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let C ∈ D(A_inf) be such that H^j(C)[1/p] is free for every j, and fix i. Then H^i(C) ⊗_{A_inf} W(k) → H^i(C ⊗^L_{A_inf} W(k)) is injective and an isomorphism after inverting p; it is an isomorphism if H^{i+1}(C) has no x-torsion.

items.name: Corollary 4.17: cohomology of perfect A_inf-complexes and its crystalline specialization
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers O, O^♭ its tilt, k the residue field, A_inf = W(O^♭), and x ∈ A_inf the Teichmüller lift of a non-zero non-unit of O^♭. Let C ∈ D(A_inf) be perfect with H^j(C)[1/p] free for all j. Then every H^j(C) is finitely presented. If H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)) is p-torsion-free, then H^i(C) is finite free, so H^i(C ⊗^L W(K^♭)) = H^i(C) ⊗ W(K^♭) is p-torsion-free; if moreover H^{i+1}(C) ⊗ W(k) is p-torsion-free (e.g. H^{i+1}(C ⊗^L W(k)) is), then H^i(C) ⊗ W(k) = H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)).
items.locator: Corollary 4.17 and the remark after it, p. 274

items.name: Lemma 4.18: torsion-freeness of the crystalline and de Rham specializations agree
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and C ∈ D(A_inf) perfect with H^j(C)[1/p] free for all j. For fixed i, H^i(C ⊗^L_{A_inf} W(k)) is p-torsion-free iff H^i(C ⊗^L_{A_inf} O) is p-torsion-free.
items.note: A finitely presented O-module M is free iff Tor_1^O(M, k) = 0.

items.name: Lemma 4.19: a criterion for M[1/p] to be finite free
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, and M a finitely presented A_inf-module with M[1/pμ] finite projective over A_inf[1/pμ] and M ⊗_{A_inf} B_crys^+ finite projective over B_crys^+. Then M[1/p] is finite free over A_inf[1/p].
items.note: The μ-adic completion of A_inf[1/p] receives a map from B_crys^+; conclude by Beauville–Laszlo and Corollary 4.12.

items.name: Corollary 4.20: the crystalline-specialization criterion with B_crys^+ hypotheses
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity and C ∈ D(A_inf) perfect with H^j(C)[1/pμ] free over A_inf[1/pμ] and H^j(C ⊗^L B_crys^+) free over B_crys^+ for all j. Then every H^j(C) is finitely presented with H^j(C)[1/p] free, and the conclusions of Corollary 4.17 hold; by Lemma 4.18 the hypotheses on H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)) may be replaced by those on H^i(C ⊗^L O).

items.name: Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field, A_inf = W(O^♭) with Frobenius φ, ξ a generator of ker θ and ξ̃ = φ(ξ). A Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module is a finitely presented A_inf-module M with an isomorphism φ_M : M ⊗_{A_inf,φ} A_inf[1/ξ̃] ≅ M[1/ξ̃] such that M[1/p] is finite projective (equivalently free) over A_inf[1/p].
items.note: AI.2 names BMS1 Definition 4.22 as its source.

items.name: BKF modules are not closed under cokernels
items.statement: Let K = C be a completed algebraic closure of Q_p and μ = [ε] − 1. Then M = A_inf/μ with the Frobenius induced from φ^*(μ) ⊂ (μ) is finitely presented and φ_M becomes an isomorphism after inverting ξ̃, but M[1/p] is not finite projective. There is a nonzero map A_inf ≅ A_inf ⊗ Z_p(1) → A_inf{1} whose cokernel is this module, so the category of Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules is not stable under cokernels; it is an exact tensor category in which the Tate twist is invertible.
items.note: AI.2 acceptance: 'a torsion/cokernel failure'.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist A_inf{1}
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field. For r ≥ 1 put W_r(O){1} := L̂_{W_r(O)/Z_p}[−1] = L_{W_r(O)/A_inf}[−1] = ξ̃_rA_inf/ξ̃_r^2A_inf, free of rank 1 over W_r(O). For r > s the natural map W_r(O){1} → W_s(O){1} has image p^{r−s}W_s(O){1}; dividing by p^{r−s}, A_inf{1} := lim_r W_r(O){1} is a free A_inf-module of rank 1 with a natural Frobenius, a BKF module. If K has characteristic 0 and contains all p-power roots of unity, with ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ), the ξ̃_r give a basis e with φ(e) = ξ̃^{−1}e, and dlog : Z_p(1) → T_p(Ω^1_{W_r(O)/Z_p}) induces A_inf ⊗ Z_p(1) → A_inf{1} with image μA_inf{1}, so A_inf{1} = μ^{−1}(A_inf ⊗_{Z_p} Z_p(1)). M{n} := M ⊗ A_inf{1}^{⊗n}.
items.note: AI.0: 'Construct Breuil–Kisin twists and their tensor powers with source orientation, distinguishing A_inf{1}, its étale Z_p(1) realization and the reduction twist (I/I²).' The BMS2 extraction compares BMS2's twist with this one.

items.name: Lemma 4.26: the étale realization of a BKF module
items.statement: Let (M, φ_M) be a BKF module over an algebraically closed field C of characteristic 0. Then T = (M ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ_M = 1} is a finitely generated Z_p-module with M ⊗ W(C^♭) = T ⊗_{Z_p} W(C^♭), and M ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf[1/μ] = T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/μ] inside the common base extension to W(C^♭).

items.name: Lemma 4.27: the crystalline specialization of a BKF module
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and M a BKF module. Then M' = M ⊗_{A_inf} W(k) is a finitely generated W(k)-module with a Frobenius automorphism after inverting p, and for a section k → O_K/p (inducing W(k) → A_inf) there is a noncanonical φ-equivariant isomorphism M ⊗_{A_inf} B_crys^+ ≅ M' ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys^+ reducing to the identity over W(k)[1/p].
items.note: Cited from Fargues–Fontaine, Corollaire 11.1.14. In geometric situations the isomorphism is canonical (Proposition 13.21).

items.name: Theorem 1.6 / 4.28 (Fargues): classification of finite free BKF modules
items.statement: Let K = C be algebraically closed of characteristic 0. The functor (M, φ_M) ↦ (T, Ξ), T = (M ⊗ W(C^♭))^{φ_M = 1}, Ξ = M ⊗_{A_inf} B_dR^+ ⊂ M ⊗ B_dR ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR, is an equivalence between finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and pairs (T, Ξ) of a finite free Z_p-module T and a B_dR^+-lattice Ξ ⊂ T ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR. The functor is exact but its inverse is not. A_inf{1} corresponds to (Z_p(1), ξ^{−1}(Z_p(1) ⊗ B_dR^+)).
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p. 224; Theorem 4.28 and the paragraphs after Remark 4.29, pp. 279–280
items.note: BMS1 refer to Scholze–Weinstein's Berkeley lectures for the proof and only need full faithfulness, which Remark 4.29 proves directly: faithfulness from Lemma 4.26, fullness by showing M ⊂ φ^{−r}(μ)^{−1}N for all r and ∩_r φ^{−r}(μ)^{−1}N = N (Lemma 3.23). AI.2 cites Definition 4.22, Lemmas 4.26–4.27 and Theorem 4.28.

items.name: Lemma 4.30: 𝔖 → A_inf is flat
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. Let C be a completed algebraic closure of K with π^♭ ∈ O_C^♭. The map 𝔖 → A_inf sending T to [π^♭]^p and restricting to the Frobenius on W(k) is flat. More generally, a map A → B of p-adically complete p-torsion-free rings with A noetherian and A/p → B/p flat is flat.

items.name: Proposition 4.32: base change of Breuil–Kisin modules to A_inf
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. The functor M ↦ M ⊗_𝔖 A_inf, with φ_M ⊗ id, is an exact tensor functor from Breuil–Kisin modules over 𝔖 to Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over A_inf; the image of E generates ker(θ̃ : A_inf → O_C).

items.name: Corollary 4.33: Kisin's functor sends Z_p(1) to 𝔖{1}
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)[[T]] with θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, T ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E, and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with T ↦ T^p. Under the functor of Theorem 4.4, Z_p(1) is sent to 𝔖{1}; indeed 𝔖{1} ⊗_𝔖 A_inf ≅ A_inf{1} as BKF modules, compatibly with the G_{K_∞}-action.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (Scholze): finiteness of p-adic étale cohomology of proper smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field, C a completed algebraic closure, and X a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety over K. Then H^i_et(X_C, Z_p) is a finitely generated Z_p-module for every i.
items.note: Cited from Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties (Forum Math. Pi 2013), Theorem 1.1, whose proof is the primitive comparison theorem; for proper smooth formal models it also follows from Theorem 14.3 here. The atlas has no layer for it; Scholze (2013) is listed as a prerequisite.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (Scholze): the de Rham comparison for proper smooth rigid spaces over discretely valued fields
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field, C a completed algebraic closure with Galois group G_K, and X a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety over K. There is a comparison isomorphism H^i_et(X_C, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X) ⊗_K B_dR, compatible with the G_K-actions and the filtrations; in particular H^i_et(X_C, Q_p) is de Rham, and H^i_dR(X) ⊗_K B_dR^+ ⊂ H^i_et(X_C, Z_p) ⊗ B_dR is a natural B_dR^+-lattice.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1 and the paragraph after it, p. 283
items.note: P8 applies CP.3–CP.4 'to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; CP.3 proves agreement with the pro-étale period-sheaf construction. BMS1 recall the proof: the Poincaré lemma for OB_dR^+ and Brinon's Galois cohomology computation.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module of the étale cohomology of a proper smooth rigid space
items.statement: For X proper smooth over C (or over a discretely valued K, base changed to C), the torsion-free quotient of H^i_et(X, Z_p) together with the B_dR^+-lattice given by de Rham cohomology (H^i_dR(X_0) ⊗_K B_dR^+ in the discretely valued case, H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) in general, Theorem 13.1) defines, by Fargues' theorem, a finite free BKF module BKF(H^i_et(X, Z_p)). If the torsion-free quotient is crystalline, BKF(H^i_et) = BK(H^i_et) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf (Proposition 4.34).
items.locator: §5, paragraphs after Theorem 5.1 and Remark 5.2, pp. 283–284
items.note: The object in which Theorems 1.4 and 14.5(iii) recover crystalline cohomology.

items.name: The pro-étale site of a locally noetherian adic space
items.statement: For a locally noetherian adic space X, X_proet is the full subcategory of pro-X_et of objects lim_i U_i with finite étale surjective transition maps, with coverings the families {f_i : U_i → U} that are pointwise surjective on |U| and such that each f_i is a transfinite composite U_i = lim_{μ<λ} U_μ with U_0 → U étale and each U_μ → lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} finite étale surjective (the corrected convention of Scholze's corrigendum). The projection ν : X_proet → X_et satisfies H^j(U, ν^*F) = colim_i H^j(U_i, F) for U = lim U_i with |U| qcqs.
items.note: AI.3: 'Use the corrected transfinite pro-étale covers … from Scholze's corrigendum'; AdicEtaleGeometry A1 constructs the elementary site with this covering convention.

items.name: Affinoid perfectoids and the toric tower (Scholze, Lemma 4.5)
items.statement: For X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), an object lim_i Spa(R_i, R_i^+) of X_proet with finite étale surjective transitions is affinoid perfectoid if the completed direct limit R = (colim R_i^+)^∧_p[1/p] is perfectoid (then R^+ = (colim R_i^+)^∧ is a perfectoid ring, Lemma 3.20); affinoid perfectoids form a basis of X_proet. If X → T^d = Spa(C⟨T_i^{±1}⟩, O⟨T_i^{±1}⟩) is étale and a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, then lim_r X ×_{T^d} T^d_r, with T^d_r obtained by adjoining T_i^{±1/p^r}, is affinoid perfectoid.
items.note: AI.3: 'Build a toric perfectoid cover of a small framed affine'. Cited from Scholze (2013), Proposition 4.8 and Lemma 4.5.

items.name: The integral period sheaves on X_proet and the maps θ_r
items.statement: On X_proet define O_X^+ = ν^*O^+_{X_et}, O_X = ν^*O_{X_et}, Ô_X^+ = lim_r O_X^+/p^r, Ô_X = Ô_X^+[1/p], Ô^+_{X^♭} = lim_φ O_X^+/p, and A_inf,X the derived p-adic completion of W(Ô^+_{X^♭}) (it is unclear whether W(Ô^+_{X^♭}) itself is derived p-complete; the defect is [𝔪^♭]-torsion). Sheafifying Lemma 3.2 gives isomorphisms W(Ô^+_{X^♭}) = lim_R W_r(Ô^+_{X^♭}) ← lim_F W_r(Ô^+_{X^♭}) → lim_F W_r(O^+_X/p) ← lim_F W_r(Ô^+_X), hence θ̃_r, θ_r = θ̃_r φ^r : A_inf,X → W_r(Ô_X^+) and θ : A_inf,X → Ô_X^+.
items.locator: Definition 5.4, Remark 5.5 and the paragraph after Lemma 5.6, pp. 285–286
items.note: AI.3: 'construct the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt and the Witt A_inf,X sheaf'.

items.name: Lemma 5.6: period sheaves on affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: Let U = lim_i Spa(R_i, R_i^+) ∈ X_proet be affinoid perfectoid with completed limit (R, R^+). Then O_X^+(U) = colim R_i^+, O_X(U) = colim R_i, Ô_X^+(U) = R^+, Ô_X(U) = R, Ô^+_{X^♭}(U) = R^{+♭} and H^0(U, A_inf,X) = A_inf(R^+). For i > 0, H^i(U, O_X) = H^i(U, Ô_X) = 0, H^i(U, O_X^+) and H^i(U, Ô_X^+) are killed by 𝔪, H^i(U, Ô^+_{X^♭}) by 𝔪^♭, and H^i(U, A_inf,X) by [𝔪^♭] (indeed by W(𝔪^♭)). The sheaves Ô_X^+ and W_r(Ô_X^+) are derived p-adically complete.
items.locator: Lemma 5.6, Remark 5.5 and the remark after Lemma 5.6, p. 286
items.note: Cited from Scholze (2013), Lemmas 4.10, 5.10 and Theorem 6.5, which rest on almost purity (PerfectoidSpaces P3) and almost acyclicity (P2).

items.name: Theorem 5.7: the primitive comparison with A_inf-coefficients
items.statement: Let C be algebraically closed and X a proper smooth adic space over C. The inclusion A_inf ↪ A_inf,X induces an almost quasi-isomorphism RΓ_et(X, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf → RΓ(X_proet, A_inf,X); more precisely the cohomology of its cone is killed by W(𝔪^♭).
items.note: Cited from the proof of Scholze (2013), Theorem 8.4 (primitive comparison), which gives [𝔪^♭]-torsion; BMS1 upgrade it to W(𝔪^♭) because the cone is derived p-complete and so a module over W(k) = A_inf/W(𝔪^♭). It feeds the étale specializations (Theorems 1.8(iv), 14.1(iv)), which AI.4 plans.

items.name: The de Rham period sheaf and its Poincaré lemma
items.statement: For a smooth rigid space X over a discretely valued K, the structural sheaf OB^+_{dR,X} (a completion of O_X ⊗_{W(k)} B^+_{dR,X}, formed as in Scholze's corrigendum) carries a connection ∇ from the O_X-factor, and 0 → B^+_{dR,X} → OB^+_{dR,X} → OB^+_{dR,X} ⊗ Ω^1_X → ⋯ is exact; the cohomology of OB^+_{dR,X}[1/ξ] is that of O_X ⊗̂_K B_dR (Brinon). Together with RΓ_et(X_C, Z_p) ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ RΓ_proet(X_C, B^+_{dR,X}) this proves Theorem 5.1.
items.locator: §5.1, closing sketch of the proof of Theorem 5.1, p. 287
items.note: P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma'. Used in §13 to compare Theorem 13.1 with Scholze's isomorphism.

items.name: Lemma 6.1: strongly K-flat resolutions
items.statement: For every complex D^• of O_T-modules on a ringed topos there is a strongly K-flat complex C^• (K-flat with flat terms) and a quasi-isomorphism C^• → D^•; hence D(O_T) is the localization of the strongly K-flat complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.
items.note: From Stacks Tag 077J and its proof. AI.1 needs it to 'prove independence of a torsionfree representative'.

items.name: The décalage η_𝓘 of an 𝓘-torsion-free complex
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. For a complex C^• with 𝓘 ⊗ C^i → C^i injective for all i, η_𝓘C^• has terms (η_𝓘C)^i = {x ∈ C^i : dx ∈ 𝓘·C^{i+1}} ⊗_{O_T} 𝓘^{⊗i} and differential induced by d. If 𝓘 = (f) with f a non-zero-divisor, (η_fC)^i = {x ∈ f^iC^i : dx ∈ f^{i+1}C^{i+1}} ⊂ C^i[1/f], and η_𝓘(C[1]) ≅ (η_𝓘C)[1] by multiplication by f.

items.name: Lemma 6.4: the cohomology of η_𝓘C kills 𝓘-torsion
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. For an 𝓘-torsion-free complex C^• there is a canonical isomorphism H^i(η_𝓘C^•) ≅ (H^i(C^•)/H^i(C^•)[𝓘]) ⊗_{O_T} 𝓘^{⊗i}, where H^i(C^•)[𝓘] is the 𝓘-torsion. In particular η_𝓘 preserves quasi-isomorphisms of 𝓘-torsion-free complexes.

items.name: Corollary 6.5: the derived functor Lη_𝓘
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. The functor η_𝓘 on strongly K-flat complexes factors canonically through a functor Lη_𝓘 : D(O_T) → D(O_T), which commutes with filtered colimits and with canonical truncations: Lη_𝓘(τ^{[a,b]}C) ≅ τ^{[a,b]}Lη_𝓘(C) for all a ≤ b in Z ∪ {±∞}. Lη_𝓘 is not exact: for 𝓘 = (p) ⊂ Z, Lη_p(Z/p) = 0 but Lη_p(Z/p^2) = Z/p.
items.note: AI.1 acceptance includes 'a case where an unjustified exactness assertion fails'.

items.name: Proposition 6.7: Lη_𝓘 is lax symmetric monoidal
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. There are natural maps Lη_𝓘C ⊗^L_{O_T} Lη_𝓘D → Lη_𝓘(C ⊗^L_{O_T} D), functorial and symmetric in C, D ∈ D(O_T), making Lη_𝓘 lax symmetric monoidal.
items.note: The same classification as the BMS2 extraction (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/042).

items.name: Proposition 6.8: Lη_f is symmetric monoidal over a valuation ring
items.statement: If T is the punctual topos, R = O_T is a valuation ring and f ∈ R generates 𝓘, then Lη_f : D(R) → D(R) is symmetric monoidal.
items.note: Reduce to perfect complexes, which split as sums of R/g[i]; then compare R/(g/f) ⊗^L R/(h/f) using Lemma 7.9.

items.name: Lemma 6.9: comparison maps between Lη_𝓘 and the identity
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. For every integer m there is a natural transformation 𝓘^{⊗m} ⊗ τ^{≤m} → τ^{≤m}Lη_𝓘 of functors on D(O_T). For every integer n there is a natural transformation τ^{≥n}Lη_𝓘 → 𝓘^{⊗n} ⊗ τ^{≥n} on the full subcategory of C with H^n(C) 𝓘-torsion-free. On that subcategory, for n ≤ m, the composites 𝓘^{⊗(m−n)} ⊗ τ^{[n,m]}Lη_𝓘 → 𝓘^{⊗m} ⊗ τ^{[n,m]} → τ^{[n,m]}Lη_𝓘 and 𝓘^{⊗m} ⊗ τ^{[n,m]} → τ^{[n,m]}Lη_𝓘 → 𝓘^{⊗n} ⊗ τ^{[n,m]} are the identity tensored with the inclusions 𝓘^{⊗(m−n)} ⊂ O_T resp. 𝓘^{⊗m} → 𝓘^{⊗n}.

items.name: Lemma 6.10: the natural map Lη_𝓘C → C for coconnective C
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. If C ∈ D^{≥0}(O_T) and H^0(C)[𝓘] = 0, there is a canonical map Lη_𝓘C → C (the case n = 0 of Lemma 6.9).

items.name: Lemma 6.11: composition of décalages
items.statement: Let 𝓘, 𝓙 ⊂ O_T be invertible ideal sheaves with product 𝓘 ⊗ 𝓙 ≅ 𝓘·𝓙 ⊂ O_T. Then Lη_{𝓘·𝓙} ≅ Lη_𝓘 ∘ Lη_𝓙 as functors D(O_T) → D(O_T).
items.note: AI.1: 'compatibility with composition in eligible elements'.

items.name: Proposition 6.12: Lη_𝓘C modulo 𝓘 is the Bockstein complex
items.statement: Let (T, O_T) be a ringed topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf. For C ∈ D(O_T) let H^•(C/𝓘) be the complex with terms H^i(C ⊗^L O_T/𝓘) ⊗ 𝓘^{⊗i} and differential the Bockstein of 0 → 𝓘/𝓘^2 → O_T/𝓘^2 → O_T/𝓘 → 0. There is a natural quasi-isomorphism Lη_𝓘C ⊗^L_{O_T} O_T/𝓘 ≃ H^•(C/𝓘); for an 𝓘-torsion-free representative C^• it is a map of complexes η_𝓘C^• ⊗ O_T/𝓘 → H^•(C/𝓘). If R^• is a differential graded algebra with 𝓘-torsion-free terms, η_𝓘R^• is a dga, H^•(R^•/𝓘) is a dga under cup product, and the quasi-isomorphism is multiplicative (Lemma 6.13).
items.note: AI.1: 'the Bockstein description modulo f; carry the Bockstein differential, not just the graded cohomology modules'. This is the property that led the authors to Lη.

items.name: Lemma 6.14: Lη commutes with flat pullback
items.statement: Let f : (T', O_{T'}) → (T, O_T) be a flat map of ringed topoi (e.g. a point, or a flat change of rings) and 𝓘' = f^*𝓘. Then Lη_{𝓘'} f^*C ≅ f^*Lη_𝓘C naturally for C ∈ D(O_T).
items.note: AI.1: 'Prove the precise base-change criterion used for AΩ'.

items.name: Lemma 6.15 (Bhatt–Scholze): derived completeness is detected on cohomology
items.statement: Let T be a replete topos and 𝓙 ⊂ O_T a locally finitely generated ideal. A complex K ∈ D(O_T) is derived 𝓙-complete iff every H^i(K) is derived 𝓙-complete; derived 𝓙-complete O_T-modules form an abelian Serre subcategory. For example a complex of p-adically complete p-torsion-free groups is derived p-complete although its cohomology need not be p-adically separated.
items.note: Cited from Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, Proposition 3.4.4 and Lemma 3.4.14. DD.1 owns derived completion and E2 the replete-topos results.

items.name: Lemma 6.17 (Bhatt–Scholze): classical versus derived completeness
items.statement: Let T be a replete topos and 𝓙 ⊂ O_T locally finitely generated. An O_T-module M is classically 𝓙-complete (M ≅ lim_k M/𝓙^k) iff it is derived 𝓙-complete and 𝓙-adically separated.
items.note: Cited from Bhatt–Scholze (2015), Proposition 3.4.2.

items.name: Lemma 6.18: cohomology of a completed direct sum
items.statement: Let 𝓙 be locally generated by one element and C_i (i ∈ I) derived 𝓙-complete complexes with H^0(C_i) classically 𝓙-complete and H^0(C_i)[𝓙^∞] = H^0(C_i)[𝓙^n] for some n independent of i. If C is the derived 𝓙-completion of ⊕_i C_i, then H^0(C) = lim_k ⊕_i H^0(C_i)/𝓙^k, the classical completion.

items.name: Lemma 6.19: Lη preserves derived completeness
items.statement: Let T be a replete topos, 𝓙 ⊂ O_T locally finitely generated and 𝓘 invertible. If C ∈ D(O_T) is derived 𝓙-complete, so is Lη_𝓘C.
items.note: AI.1 names Lemma 6.19 explicitly.

items.name: Lemma 6.20: Lη_𝓘 commutes with 𝓘-adic completion
items.statement: Let T be a replete topos and 𝓘 ⊂ O_T an invertible ideal sheaf, and C ∈ D(O_T) with derived 𝓘-completion Ĉ. Then the natural maps (Lη_𝓘C)^∧ → Lη_𝓘Ĉ → R lim_n Lη_𝓘(C ⊗^L O_T/𝓘^n) are quasi-isomorphisms. (For a different ideal 𝓙, Lη_𝓘 need not commute with 𝓙-adic completion.)
items.note: AI.1 names Lemma 6.20 explicitly and asks for a regression example of the unrestricted claim.

items.name: Koszul complexes of commuting endomorphisms
items.statement: For an abelian group M with commuting endomorphisms f_1, …, f_d, the Koszul complex K_M(f_1, …, f_d) is M → ⊕_i M → ⊕_{i<j} M → ⋯, whose component from the spot i_1 < ⋯ < i_k to j_1 < ⋯ < j_{k+1} ⊃ {i_1, …, i_k} is (−1)^{m−1}f_{j_m} for the unique j_m not among the i's; equivalently M ⊗_{Z[f]} ⊗_i (Z[f] →^{f_i} Z[f]), in cohomological degrees [0, d], independent of the order of the f_i. It computes M ⊗^L_{Z[f_1,…,f_d]} Z up to a shift by d. For R = A[x_1, …, x_d] and f_i = ∂/∂x_i it is the de Rham complex Ω^•_{R/A}.
items.locator: Definition 7.1, the paragraph after it and Example 7.2, p. 298
items.note: AI.1: 'Prove the Koszul calculation for commuting endomorphisms'.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: Koszul complexes compute group cohomology of Z^d and Z_p^d
items.statement: Let Γ_disc = Z^d with generators γ_1, …, γ_d and Γ = Z_p^d. (i) For a Γ_disc-module M, RΓ(Γ_disc, M) is computed by K_M(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1). (ii) If N = lim_k N_k with N_k continuous discrete Γ-modules killed by p^k, then RΓ_cont(Γ, N) → RΓ(Γ_disc, N) is a quasi-isomorphism, so RΓ_cont(Γ, N) is computed by K_N(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1). Replacing γ_i by c(i)γ_i with c(i) ∈ Z_p^× gives canonically isomorphic Koszul complexes.
items.note: AI.1: 'Prove the Koszul calculation for commuting endomorphisms and integral continuous cochains.'

items.name: Lemma 7.5: the multiplicative structure on Koszul complexes of group cohomology
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, R an A-algebra (not necessarily commutative) and Γ_disc = Z^d acting on R by A-algebra automorphisms. Then K_R(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1) is naturally a differential graded A-algebra — generated by R and degree-one x_i with x_ix_j = −x_jx_i, x_i^2 = 0, x_ir = γ_i(r)x_i, dx_i = 0, dr = Σ(γ_i(r) − r)x_i — and the quasi-isomorphism with RΓ(Γ_disc, R) is one of algebra objects of D(A); it induces the cup product. The dga is not commutative even if R is, but K_R/f is commutative if Γ acts trivially on R/f.

items.name: The q-de Rham complex of a Laurent polynomial ring
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring with a unit q and R = A[T^{±1}] with γ : T ↦ qT. Then η_{q−1}(R →^{γ−1} R) is the q-de Rham complex q-Ω^•_{A[T^{±1}]/A} : A[T^{±1}] → A[T^{±1}] dlog_q T, T^n ↦ [n]_q T^n dlog_q T, with [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1); in closed form f(T) ↦ (f(qT) − f(T))/(qT − T) d_qT. It is a differential graded algebra with dlog_q T · f(T) = f(qT) · dlog_q T. In d variables q-Ω^•_{A[T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/A} = ⊗_i q-Ω^•_{A[T_i^{±1}]/A} = η_{q−1}K(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1) computes Lη_{q−1}RΓ(Z^d, A[T^{±1}]). It depends on the coordinates.
items.note: PR.6 constructs framed q-de Rham complexes (BS22 §16); AI.3 identifies AΩ locally with them.

items.name: Remark 7.8: the q-de Rham complex is not a commutative dga
items.statement: Take A = F_2[q^{±1}] and R = A[T^{±1}] with γ : T ↦ qT; let E_2 = RΓ(Z, R) and E_1 = Lη_{q−1}E_2 as E_∞-A-algebras (using that RΓ(Z, −) and Lη_{q−1} are lax symmetric monoidal and E_1 → E_2 is a map of E_∞-algebras). Then the E_∞-F_2-algebra E_1 cannot be modelled by a commutative differential graded F_2-algebra: the Steenrod operation Sq^0, φ-linear on E_∞-A-algebras and vanishing on H^{>0} of cdgas, satisfies Sq^0(dlog_q T) ↦ (q − 1)^2 x ≠ 0 in H^1(E_2). Hence AΩ_R, and even AΩ_R/p, is not a cdga for R = O⟨T^{±1}⟩.
items.note: The printed remark defines E_1 = Lη_{q−1}E_1; the intended E_1 = Lη_{q−1}E_2 (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 7.9: Lη on Koszul complexes
items.statement: Let f be a non-zero-divisor of a ring R, M^• a complex of f-torsion-free R-modules, and g_1, …, g_m ∈ R non-zero-divisors each divisible by f or dividing f. If some g_i divides f, then η_f(M^• ⊗_R K_R(g_1, …, g_m)) is acyclic. If f divides every g_i, then η_fK_R(g_1, …, g_m) ≅ K_R(g_1/f, …, g_m/f) and η_f(M^• ⊗_R K_R(g_1, …, g_m)) ≅ η_fM^• ⊗_R K_R(g_1/f, …, g_m/f) as complexes.
items.note: AI.1's 'Koszul calculation'. The proof's explicit model has a misprint (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 7.10: cohomology of Koszul complexes when g is null-homotopic
items.statement: Let g ∈ R. (i) If multiplication by g on a complex M^• is null-homotopic, the long exact sequence for M^• ⊗_R K_R(g) splits into split short exact sequences 0 → H^{n−1}(M^•) → H^n(M^• ⊗ K_R(g)) → H^n(M^•) → 0. (ii) If g_1, …, g_m ∈ R are all divisible by g and some g_i is g times a unit, then for every R-module M, H^n(K_M(g_1, …, g_m)) ≅ Ann_M(g)^{⊕C(m−1,n)} ⊕ (M/gM)^{⊕C(m−1,n−1)}.

items.name: The complex Ω̃_𝔛 and the twist O{1}
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. Ω̃_𝔛 := Lη_{ζ_p−1}(Rν_*Ô_X^+) ∈ D(𝔛_Zar), independent of the choice of ζ_p and a commutative O_𝔛-algebra in D(𝔛_Zar). O{1} := T_p(Ω^1_{O/Z_p}) = L̂_{O/Z_p}[−1] = L_{O/A_inf}[−1] = ξ̃A_inf/ξ̃^2A_inf is free of rank one over O = A_inf/ξ̃ and contains O(1) with cokernel killed exactly by (ζ_p − 1); a choice of roots of unity trivializes it by ((ζ_p − 1)^{−1} dζ_{p^r}/ζ_{p^r})_r; M{n} := M ⊗_O O{n}.
items.note: Ω̃_𝔛 is the Hodge–Tate specialization AΩ_𝔛 ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃} O (Theorem 9.2(i)), which AI.4 plans; O{1} is the reduction of A_inf{1} (AI.0).

items.name: Theorem 8.3: the Hodge–Tate (integral Cartier) isomorphism
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. There is a natural isomorphism H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ Ω^{i,cont}_{𝔛/O}{−i} of sheaves on 𝔛_Zar, where Ω^{i,cont}_{𝔛/O} = lim_n Ω^i_{(𝔛/p^n)/(O/p^n)}. In particular Ω̃_𝔛 is a perfect complex of O_𝔛-modules.
items.locator: Theorem 8.3, p. 305; proof completed after Proposition 8.15, p. 313
items.note: AI.4: 'Prove the Hodge–Tate reduction of AΩ along tilde-theta, identifying its cohomology sheaves with differential forms and BK twists.' A mixed-characteristic Cartier isomorphism; Lη_{ζ_p−1} turns the almost description of Rν_*Ô_X^+ into an exact one.

items.name: Ω̃_𝔛 and liftings to A_inf/ξ̃^2
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. τ^{≤1}Ω̃_𝔛 is canonically the p-adic completion of L_{𝔛/Z_p}[−1]{−1}, an extension of Ω^{1,cont}_{𝔛/O}{−1}[−1] by O_𝔛 whose Ext^2-class is the obstruction to lifting 𝔛 to A_inf/ξ̃^2. So if 𝔛 does not lift to A_inf/ξ̃^2, Ω̃_𝔛 is not a direct sum of its cohomology sheaves (an integral analogue of Deligne–Illusie).

items.name: Small algebras, framings and the perfectoid cover R_∞
items.statement: A formally smooth O-algebra R is small (Faltings) if there is an étale map □ : Spf R → Ĝ_m^d = Spf O⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ (a framing). Then R_∞ = R ⊗̂_{O⟨T^{±1}⟩} O⟨T_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, T_d^{±1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid, integrally closed in R_∞[1/p], the corresponding tower is affinoid perfectoid in X_proet, and Γ = Z_p(1)^d acts, γ_i sending T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ ζ_{p^m}T_i^{1/p^m} and fixing the other T_j. Every sufficiently small Zariski open of 𝔛 is of this form.
items.locator: Definition 8.5 and the paragraphs after it, pp. 306–307
items.note: AI.3: 'Build a toric perfectoid cover of a small framed affine, compute its continuous group cochains'.

items.name: Local variants Ω̃_R^□, Ω̃_R^profet, Ω̃_R^proet
items.statement: For R small with framing □ and X its generic fibre: Ω̃_R^□ = Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ_cont(Γ, R_∞), Ω̃_R^profet = Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ(X_profet, Ô_X^+) and Ω̃_R^proet = Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ(X_proet, Ô_X^+), with natural maps Ω̃_R^□ → Ω̃_R^profet → Ω̃_R^proet → RΓ(𝔛, Ω̃_𝔛); the first two are almost quasi-isomorphisms by almost purity. If Spf R is connected, RΓ(X_profet, Ô_X^+) = RΓ_cont(Δ, R̂̄) for Δ the Galois group of the maximal pro-finite étale extension of R[1/p].
items.locator: Definition 8.6 and the paragraphs around it, p. 307

items.name: Theorem 8.7 and Corollary 8.13: the local Hodge–Tate comparison
items.statement: Let R be a small formally smooth O-algebra with framing □. (i) The maps Ω̃_R^□ → Ω̃_R^profet → Ω̃_R^proet → RΓ(𝔛, Ω̃_𝔛) are quasi-isomorphisms; write Ω̃_R for the common value. (ii) There are natural isomorphisms H^i(Ω̃_R) ≅ Ω^{i,cont}_{R/O}{−i}; for the framing, R^d ≅ H^1(Ω̃_R) and its exterior powers give ∧^iR^d ≅ H^i(Ω̃_R). (iii) For a formally étale map R → R' of small algebras, Ω̃_R ⊗^L_R R' ≃ Ω̃_{R'}. Without smallness the maps are only known to be almost quasi-isomorphisms.

items.name: Proposition 8.9: continuous cohomology of R_∞ and its lack of almost zero elements
items.statement: For R small with framing and all i ≥ 0, ∧^iR^d = H^i_cont(Γ, R) → H^i_cont(Γ, R_∞) is split injective with cokernel killed by ζ_p − 1; the cokernel is R ⊗_O ⊕_{0≠a∈(Z[1/p]∩[0,1))^d} H^i_cont(Γ, O·T^a). Moreover H^i_cont(Γ, R_∞) and H^i_cont(Γ, R_∞)/(ζ_p − 1) have no almost zero elements (none killed by 𝔪).
items.note: AI.3: 'Separate the integral component of the toric cochains from nonintegral monomials and prove the annihilation estimates'. Uses Scholze (2013) Lemma 5.5 and Corollary 3.29.

items.name: Lemma 8.10: formally smooth O-algebras are topologically free
items.statement: Every formally smooth O-algebra R is the p-adic completion of a free O-module.
items.note: For r large, R/(ζ_{p^r} − 1) ≅ R_k ⊗_k O/(ζ_{p^r} − 1) after fixing a section k → O/p; lift a basis.

items.name: Lemma 8.11: Lη turns suitable almost isomorphisms into isomorphisms
