items.statement: Let A be a ring, I ⊂ A an ideal and f ∈ I a non-zero-divisor. (i) If M is an A-module such that M and M/f have no non-zero elements killed by I, and α : M → N has kernel and cokernel killed by I, then M/M[f] → N/N[f] is an isomorphism. (ii) If g : C → D in D(A) has all H^i(g) with kernel and cokernel killed by I, and every H^i(C) and H^i(C)/f has no non-zero element killed by I, then Lη_fg is a quasi-isomorphism. (No hypothesis on D is needed; without hypotheses on C it fails, e.g. 𝔪 → O for A = O, I = 𝔪, f = ζ_p − 1.)
items.note: AI.3: 'Show exactly how Lη upgrades the needed almost comparison; an almost isomorphism is not itself an integral isomorphism.'

items.name: Proposition 8.14: Künneth formula for Ω̃
items.statement: For small formally smooth O-algebras R_1, R_2 and R = R_1 ⊗̂_O R_2, the natural map Ω̃_{R_1} ⊗̂^L_O Ω̃_{R_2} → Ω̃_R is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Reduce to tori; RΓ_cont(Γ_1 × Γ_2, −) is a tensor product of Koszul complexes and Lη_{ζ_p−1} is symmetric monoidal over O (Proposition 6.8) and commutes with completion (Lemma 6.20).

items.name: Proposition 8.15: τ^{≤1}Ω̃_R is the shifted cotangent complex
items.statement: Let R be small formally smooth over O with generic fibre X. The map L̂_{R/Z_p}[−1]{−1} → RΓ(X_proet, Ô_X^+), obtained from the transitivity triangle for Z_p → O → Ô_X^+ and L̂_{Ô_X^+/O} ≃ 0 (Lemma 3.14), factors uniquely through Ω̃_R = Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ(X_proet, Ô_X^+) and induces an equivalence L̂_{R/Z_p}[−1]{−1} ≃ τ^{≤1}Ω̃_R. In particular Ω^{1,cont}_{R/O}{−1} ≅ H^1(Ω̃_R) canonically.
items.locator: Proposition 8.15 and the paragraph after it, p. 313

items.name: Lemma 8.16: uniqueness of factorizations through Lη
items.statement: Let f be a non-zero-divisor of a ring A and α : C → D in D(A) with H^i(C) = 0 for i > 1, H^i(D) = 0 for i < 0 and H^0(D) f-torsion-free. Then α factors through the natural map Lη_fD → D (Lemma 6.10) in at most one way, and a factorization exists iff H^1(C ⊗^L A/f) → H^1(D ⊗^L A/f) vanishes, iff H^1(C) → H^1(D) factors through fH^1(D).

items.name: Proposition 8.17: the image of dlog T in the cohomology of the torus
items.statement: Let R = O⟨T^{±1}⟩, R_∞ = O⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and Γ = Z_p(1). Under RΓ_cont(Γ, L̂_{R_∞/Z_p}) = RΓ_cont(Γ, R_∞)[1]{1}, the image of dlog(T) ∈ H^0(L̂_{R/Z_p}) in H^1_cont(Γ, R_∞){1} is the image of dlog ⊗ 1 ∈ H^1_cont(Γ, O{1}) ⊗_O R, where dlog ∈ Hom_cont(Γ, T_p(Ω^1_{O/Z_p})) is induced by dlog : μ_{p^∞}(O) → Ω^1_{O/Z_p}; it generates (ζ_p − 1)H^1_cont(Γ, O{1}) ⊗ R.
items.locator: Proposition 8.17 and the paragraph after it, p. 316

items.name: The complex AΩ_𝔛
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. With μ = [ε] − 1 (the ideal (μ) is independent of ε by Lemma 3.23), AΩ_𝔛 := Lη_μ(Rν_*A_inf,X) ∈ D(𝔛_Zar), a commutative algebra over the constant sheaf A_inf in D(𝔛_Zar) (Proposition 6.7).
items.note: Same classification as BS22's extraction (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/94, planned AI.3 and AI.7).

items.name: Theorem 9.2(i),(ii): specializations of AΩ along θ̃_r
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. (i) AΩ_𝔛 ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃} O → Lη_{ζ_p−1}(Rν_*Ô_X^+) = Ω̃_𝔛 is a quasi-isomorphism. (ii) For every r ≥ 1, AΩ_𝔛 ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃_r} W_r(O) → Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}(Rν_*W_r(Ô_X^+)) =: W̃_rΩ_𝔛 is a quasi-isomorphism. Moreover AΩ_R = R lim_r W̃_rΩ_R.

items.name: Theorem 9.2(iii) / 11.1: the cohomology of W̃_rΩ is the de Rham–Witt complex
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, O = O_K, and 𝔛 a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O (locally Spf R with R p-adically complete, flat over O and R/p smooth over O/p; by Elkik, R is the p-adic completion of a smooth O-algebra) with generic fibre X and ν : X_proet → 𝔛_Zar. For r ≥ 1 and i ∈ Z there is a natural isomorphism H^i(W̃_rΩ_𝔛) ≅ W_rΩ^{i,cont}_{𝔛/O}{−i} of sheaves on 𝔛_Zar, where W_rΩ^{i,cont}_{𝔛/O} = lim_n W_rΩ^i_{(𝔛/p^n)/(O/p^n)} is the continuous relative de Rham–Witt sheaf of Langer–Zink and {−i} a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist. Locally, for R small, H^i(W̃_rΩ_R) ≅ W_rΩ^{i,cont}_{R/O}{−i}, compatibly with d, F, R, V and products; for r = 1 this is Theorem 8.3.
items.locator: Lemma 1.19, p. 232; Theorem 9.2(iii), Theorem 9.4(iv), pp. 317–318; Theorem 11.1, p. 342
items.note: AI.4: 'Construct the relative de Rham–Witt comparison using CR.4's Langer–Zink objects and the universal Witt-complex maps.' The proof is §11 (items 158–166).

items.name: Local variants of W̃_rΩ and AΩ
items.statement: For R small with framing □ and Γ = Z_p(1)^d acting on R_∞: W̃_rΩ_R^□ = Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}RΓ_cont(Γ, W_r(R_∞)), W̃_rΩ_R^profet and W̃_rΩ_R^proet with RΓ(X_profet, W_r(Ô_X^+)) and RΓ(X_proet, W_r(Ô_X^+)); AΩ_R^□ = Lη_μRΓ_cont(Γ, A_inf(R_∞)), AΩ_R^profet = Lη_μRΓ(X_profet, A_inf,X) and AΩ_R^proet = Lη_μRΓ(X_proet, A_inf,X).

items.name: Theorem 9.4(i)–(iii), Corollary 9.11 and Proposition 9.14: the local computation of AΩ and W̃_rΩ
items.statement: Let R be small with framing □ and 𝔛 = Spf R. (i) AΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃_r} W_r(O) → W̃_rΩ_R^□ is a quasi-isomorphism. (ii) W̃_rΩ_R^□ → W̃_rΩ_R^profet → W̃_rΩ_R^proet → RΓ(𝔛, W̃_rΩ_𝔛) are quasi-isomorphisms (common value W̃_rΩ_R). (iii) AΩ_R^□ → AΩ_R^profet → AΩ_R^proet → RΓ(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛) are quasi-isomorphisms (common value AΩ_R).
items.locator: Lemma 1.16 and Lemma 1.19, pp. 230–232; Theorem 9.4(i)–(iii), p. 318; Corollary 9.11, p. 327; Proposition 9.14, p. 330
items.note: AI.3: 'Prove framing independence, restriction/sheaf descent and functoriality'. The 'key lemma' of the introduction; its proof uses Lemmas 8.11 and 9.12 to turn Faltings' almost purity into honest quasi-isomorphisms.

items.name: The framed lift A(R)^□ and its q-de Rham complex
items.statement: For R small with framing □, A(R)^□ is the unique (p, μ)-adically complete A_inf-algebra formally étale over A_inf⟨U_1^{±1}, …, U_d^{±1}⟩ lifting R along θ : A_inf → O (U_i ↦ T_i). The action γ_i(U_i) = [ε]U_i (fixing U_j, j ≠ i) lifts uniquely to A(R)^□, trivially modulo [ε] − 1, giving q-derivations ∂_q/∂_q log(U_i) = (γ_i − 1)/([ε] − 1). The q-de Rham complex is q-Ω^•_{A(R)^□/A_inf} = K_{A(R)^□}(∂_q/∂_q log(U_1), …, ∂_q/∂_q log(U_d)); for R = O⟨T^{±1}⟩ it is the (p, μ)-adic completion of q-Ω^•_{A_inf[U^{±1}]/A_inf}.

items.name: Theorem 1.17 / Lemma 9.6: AΩ_R is computed by the q-de Rham complex
items.statement: Let R be small with framing □. There are injective quasi-isomorphisms q-Ω^•_{A(R)^□/A_inf} = η_{q−1}K_{A(R)^□}(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1) → AΩ_R^□ = η_{q−1}K_{A_inf(R_∞)}(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1) and q-Ω^•_{A(R)^□/A_inf}/ξ̃_r → W̃_rΩ_R^□, where q = [ε], using A(R)^□ ⊗̂_{A_inf⟨U^{±1}⟩} A_inf⟨U^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ A_inf(R_∞), U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [(T_i^{1/p^r}, T_i^{1/p^{r+1}}, …)]. The q-de Rham complex has ξ̃_r-torsion-free terms, so AΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_{θ̃_r} W_r(O) ≃ W̃_rΩ_R^□. For R = O⟨T^{±1}⟩ the differential is ∂_q/∂_qT : T^i ↦ [i]_qT^{i−1}.
items.note: Same classification as BS22's extraction (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/83: 'Comparison with the A_inf-cohomology of BMS1', planned PR.6 and AI.3). The nonintegral part is killed because multiplication by φ^{−1}(μ) is null-homotopic on it.

items.name: Lemma 9.7: the Koszul complex computing RΓ_cont(Γ, W_r(R_∞))
items.statement: Let R be small with framing and C^• = K_{W_r(R_∞)}(γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1). (i) C^• is a completed direct sum of Koszul complexes K_{W_r(O)}([ζ^{a_1}] − 1, …, [ζ^{a_d}] − 1) (ζ^{b/p^a} := ζ_{p^a}^b) for a_1, …, a_d ∈ Z[1/p], tensored with the topologically free W_r(O)-module A(R)^□/ξ_r. (ii) The groups H^i(W̃_rΩ_R^□) = H^i(η_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}C^•) are p-torsion-free. (iii) For every perfect E ∈ D(W_r(O)), H^i(C^• ⊗^L E) and H^i(C^• ⊗^L E)/([ζ_{p^r}] − 1) have no elements killed by W_r(𝔪).

items.name: Lemma 9.8: Witt vectors of (Laurent) polynomial rings
items.statement: For any ring S there are natural inclusions W_r(S[T_1^{p^r}, …, T_d^{p^r}]) ⊂ W_r(S)[U_1, …, U_d] ⊂ W_r(S[T_1, …, T_d]) with U_i = [T_i], and likewise for Laurent polynomials; hence W_r(S[T_i^{1/p^∞}]) = W_r(S)[U_i^{1/p^∞}] and W_r(S[T_i^{±1/p^∞}]) = W_r(S)[U_i^{±1/p^∞}].
items.note: From Langer–Zink, Corollary 2.4, by localization.

items.name: Lemma 9.9: étale base change for W̃_rΩ
items.statement: Let R be small with framing □ and R → R' formally étale (R/p^n → R'/p^n étale for all n, R' p-adically complete), with the induced framing □'. Then W̃_rΩ_R^□ ⊗̂^L_{W_r(R)} W_r(R') → W̃_rΩ_{R'}^{□'} is a quasi-isomorphism; modulo p^n the tensor product is underived (Remark 9.10, via Elkik and Theorem 10.4).

items.name: Lemma 9.12: when Lη_μ of an almost quasi-isomorphism over A_inf is a quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: Let f : C → D be a map of derived p-complete complexes in D(A_inf) such that (i) f ⊗^L_{Z_p} F_p is an almost quasi-isomorphism in D(O^♭); (ii) H^i(Lη_μf) is injective for all i; (iii) ∩_{m∈W(𝔪^♭), m|μ} (μ/m)H^i(C) = μH^i(C) for all i. Then Lη_μf is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: W(𝔪^♭)^2 ≠ W(𝔪^♭) in general, so 'almost' has to be handled with care; the only known m ∈ W(𝔪^♭) dividing μ are the φ^{−r}(μ).

items.name: Lemma 9.13: the intersection property for RΓ_cont(Γ, A_inf(R_∞))
items.statement: For R small with framing and C = RΓ_cont(Γ, A_inf(R_∞)) ∈ D(A_inf), ∩_{m∈W(𝔪^♭), m|μ} (μ/m)H^i(C) = μH^i(C) for all i.

items.name: An inverse limit of sheaves is a sheaf
items.statement: Let 𝔛^psh_Zar be the presheaf topos on affine opens of 𝔛 and j : 𝔛_Zar → 𝔛^psh_Zar. If C_r ∈ D(𝔛^psh_Zar), r ≥ 1, is a projective system with each C_r → Rj_*j^*C_r a quasi-isomorphism, then so is C = R lim C_r → Rj_*j^*C.
items.note: Used to deduce Proposition 9.14 from the W̃_rΩ case, since AΩ_R is not a module over R or W_r(R).

items.name: Lemma 9.16: Künneth formula for AΩ
items.statement: For small formally smooth O-algebras R_1, R_2 and R = R_1 ⊗̂_O R_2, the natural map AΩ_{R_1} ⊗̂^L_{A_inf} AΩ_{R_2} → AΩ_R is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Both sides are derived ξ̃-complete; modulo ξ̃ it is Proposition 8.14.

items.name: Proposition 9.17: the Frobenius on AΩ
items.statement: For R small formally smooth over O there is a natural φ-linear map φ : AΩ_R → AΩ_R factoring as a φ-linear quasi-isomorphism AΩ_R ≃ Lη_ξ̃AΩ_R followed by the natural map Lη_ξ̃AΩ_R → AΩ_R; for a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over O there is likewise φ : AΩ_𝔛 → AΩ_𝔛 factoring through a φ-linear quasi-isomorphism AΩ_𝔛 ≃ Lη_ξ̃AΩ_𝔛.
items.note: AI.3: 'construct Frobenius and multiplication'. Proof: φ_X is an automorphism of RΓ_proet(X, A_inf,X) and φ^*Lη_μ = Lη_{φ(μ)}φ^* = Lη_ξ̃Lη_μφ^*.

items.name: Lemma 9.18: Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1} is symmetric monoidal on W̃_rΩ
items.statement: Let R be small, D = RΓ_proet(X, W_r(Ô_X^+)) (or any complex receiving an almost quasi-isomorphism from RΓ_cont(Γ, W_r(R_∞))) and E ∈ D(W_r(O)). Then Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}D ⊗^L_{W_r(O)} Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}E → Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}(D ⊗^L_{W_r(O)} E) is a quasi-isomorphism.

items.name: Lemma 10.1: powers of Witt ideals are intertwined
items.statement: Let I be an ideal of a ring A generated by a finite set Σ, W_r(I) = ker(W_r(A) → W_r(A/I)) and [I] the ideal generated by Teichmüller lifts of I. Then W_r(I^{|Σ|p^rs}) ⊂ ⟨[a^s] : a ∈ Σ⟩ ⊂ [I]^s ⊂ [I^s] ⊂ W_r(I^s) and [I]^s ⊂ W_r(I)^s ⊂ W_r(I^s) for all s ≥ 1, so the five chains ⟨[a^s]⟩, [I]^s, [I^s], W_r(I)^s, W_r(I^s) are intertwined.

items.name: Corollary 10.2: Witt vectors of an almost-setting ideal
items.statement: If I ⊂ A satisfies I = I^2 and is an increasing union of principal ideals generated by non-zero-divisors, then W_r(I) = [I], and W_r(I) ⊂ W_r(A) again satisfies W_r(I)^2 = W_r(I) and is an increasing union of principal ideals generated by non-zero-divisors (e.g. W_r(𝔪) ⊂ W_r(O) for a perfectoid field).

items.name: Lemma 10.3: [p]-adic and p-adic topologies on W_r(A) agree
items.statement: For any ring A, [p]^{2s}W_r(A) ⊂ p^sW_r(A), p^{rs}W_r(A) ⊂ W_r(pA)^s and W_r(pA)^{p^rs} ⊂ [p]^sW_r(A); so the chains [p]^sW_r(A), W_r(pA)^s and p^sW_r(A) are intertwined.

items.name: Theorem 10.4 (van der Kallen, Langer–Zink, Borger): Witt vectors preserve étale maps
items.statement: If A → B is étale then W_r(A) → W_r(B) is étale, and for any A → A' with B' = B ⊗_A A' the map W_r(A') ⊗_{W_r(A)} W_r(B) → W_r(B') is an isomorphism.
items.note: The input to CR.4's 'localization and étale descent' for de Rham–Witt forms. BMS1 deduce the general case from Langer–Zink's F-finite case (Corollary A.18) by noetherian approximation; also van der Kallen (1986) and Borger (2011, Theorem 9.2, Corollary 9.4).

items.name: F-V-procomplexes
items.statement: Let A be a Z_(p)-algebra and B an A-algebra. An F-V-procomplex for B/A is a system (𝒲_r^•, R, F, V, λ_r)_{r≥1}: commutative dg W_r(A)-algebras 𝒲_r^•; maps R : 𝒲_{r+1}^• → R_*𝒲_r^• of dg W_{r+1}(A)-algebras; F : 𝒲_{r+1}^• → F_*𝒲_r^• of graded W_{r+1}(A)-algebras; V : F_*𝒲_r^• → 𝒲_{r+1}^• of graded W_{r+1}(A)-modules; λ_r : W_r(B) → 𝒲_r^0 commuting with F, R, V; such that R commutes with F and V, FV = p, FdV = d, V(F(x)y) = xV(y), and Fdλ_{r+1}([b]) = λ_r([b])^{p−1}dλ_r([b]) for b ∈ B (automatic if 𝒲_r^1 is p-torsion-free). Here R is regarded as the subtle operator, as in topological cyclic homology.

items.name: Theorem 10.7 (Langer–Zink): the relative de Rham–Witt complex
items.statement: For a Z_(p)-algebra A and an A-algebra B there is an initial object {W_rΩ^•_{B/A}}_r in the category of F-V-procomplexes for B/A: for any F-V-procomplex (𝒲_r^•, R, F, V, λ_r) there are unique maps of dg W_r(A)-algebras W_rΩ^•_{B/A} → 𝒲_r^• compatible with R, F, V and equal to λ_r in degree 0.
items.note: CR.4: 'Construct the relative Langer–Zink theory … This relative version … supplies BMS1 §§10–12.'

items.name: Lemma 10.8: étale base change for relative de Rham–Witt forms
items.statement: Let A → R be a map of Z_(p)-algebras and R' an étale R-algebra. Then W_rΩ^n_{R/A} ⊗_{W_r(R)} W_r(R') → W_rΩ^n_{R'/A} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Langer–Zink, Proposition 1.7, under their F-finiteness or p-nilpotence hypothesis, which BMS1 remove using Theorem 10.4; the printed proof names the hypothesis on 'S' (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 10.9 and Corollary 10.10: de Rham–Witt forms of quotients
items.statement: Let A → R be a map of Z_(p)-algebras, I ⊂ R an ideal and W_rΩ^n_{(R,I)/A} = ker(W_rΩ^n_{R/A} → W_rΩ^n_{(R/I)/A}). (i) ⊕_n W_rΩ^n_{(R,I)/A} is the dg ideal generated by W_r(I). (ii) If I is generated by a finite set Σ, the chains ⟨[a^s] : a ∈ Σ⟩W_rΩ^•_{R/A} and W_rΩ^•_{(R,I^s)/A} are intertwined. Hence for a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ A, {W_rΩ^•_{R/A} ⊗_{W_r(A)} W_r(A)/[I^s]}_s → {W_rΩ^•_{(R/I^sR)/(A/I^s)}}_s is an isomorphism of pro-dg algebras.
items.note: Part (i) follows Geisser–Hesselholt's argument for the absolute de Rham–Witt complex.

items.name: The continuous relative de Rham–Witt complex
items.statement: For a map A → R of Z_(p)-algebras, W_rΩ^{i,cont}_{R/A} := lim_s W_rΩ^i_{(R/p^s)/(A/p^s)} = lim_s W_rΩ^i_{R/A}/p^s (by Corollary 10.10 and Lemma 10.3); it is again an F-V-procomplex for R/A.
items.note: CR.4: 'Prove finite-level and inverse-limit comparisons'.

items.name: Theorem 10.12 (Langer–Zink): the basis of W_rΩ^n of a Laurent polynomial algebra
items.statement: For weights a : {1, …, d} → p^{−r}Z with u(a) = max(−v(a), 0) and the admissible partitions (I_0, …, I_n) ∈ P_a (ordered by the p-adic valuations of a, with a fixed tie-breaking order), the elements e(x, a, I_0, …, I_n) — products of V^{−v(a|I_0)}(x∏[T_i]^{…}), dV^{−v(a|I_j)}∏[T_i]^{…}, F^{v(a|I_j)}d∏[T_i]^{…} and dlog ∏[T_i] according to the sign of v(a|I_j) — define an isomorphism of W_r(A)-modules ⊕_a ⊕_{P_a} V^{u(a)}W_{r−u(a)}(A) ≅ W_rΩ^n_{A[T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/A}.
items.note: CR.4: 'Compute polynomial basic Witt differentials, localization'. Langer–Zink, Proposition 2.17, for polynomials; the Laurent case follows by localization at [T_1], …, [T_d].

items.name: Theorem 10.13 (Langer–Zink): the integral part of W_rΩ of a torus
items.statement: The map τ : Ω^•_{W_r(A)[U_1^{±1},…,U_d^{±1}]/W_r(A)} → W_rΩ^•_{A[T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/A}, U_i ↦ [T_i], is an injective quasi-isomorphism onto the integral part (the dg subalgebra generated by the [T_i]^{±1}, i.e. the weights with values in Z); the part of weight a with v(a) < 0 is acyclic. The integral part depends on the coordinates.
items.note: From the proof of Langer–Zink, Theorem 3.5.

items.name: Proposition 10.14: de Rham–Witt complexes over perfectoid bases
items.statement: Let A → A' be a map of perfectoid rings, R a smooth A-algebra and R' = R ⊗_A A'. (i) W_rΩ^n_{R/A} and W_r(A') are Tor-independent over W_r(A). (ii) W_rΩ^•_{R/A} ⊗_{W_r(A)} W_r(A') → W_rΩ^•_{R'/A'} is an isomorphism of dg W_r(A')-algebras. (Applied to O → k.)

items.name: The F-V-structure on H^•(D/ξ̃_r)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid ring, ξ a generator of ker θ with θ_r(ξ) = V(1) for all r (so θ_r(ξ̃) = p), and D ∈ D(A_inf(S)) a commutative algebra with H^i(D) = H^i(D/ξ) = 0 for i < 0 and a φ-linear automorphism φ_D. Put 𝒲_r^n(D)_pre = H^n(D ⊗^L_{A_inf(S)} A_inf(S)/ξ̃_r), a graded W_r(S)-algebra with Bockstein differential for 0 → D/ξ̃_r →^{ξ̃_r} D/ξ̃_r^2 → D/ξ̃_r → 0; let R' be induced by φ_D^{−1}, F by the projection A_inf/ξ̃_{r+1} → A_inf/ξ̃_r, V by multiplication by φ^{r+1}(ξ), and R := θ̃_r(ξ)^nR' on 𝒲^n. Then 𝒲_r^•(D)_pre is a dg W_r(S)-algebra with xy = (−1)^{|x||y|}yx; R' is a map of graded algebras and R one of dg algebras; V is additive, commutes with R and R', and V(F(x)y) = xV(y); F is a ring map commuting with R, R'; FdV = d; FV = p. Given compatible λ_r : W_r(B) → 𝒲_r^0(D)_pre for an S-algebra B satisfying the Teichmüller rule, and if x^2 = 0 for odd |x|, this is an F-V-procomplex for B/S and receives W_rΩ^•_{B/S}; but then im λ_r^n ⊂ ∩_s θ̃_r(ξ_s)^n𝒲_r^n(D)_pre, which is too small.
items.note: AI.4: 'using … the universal Witt-complex maps'.

items.name: Proposition 11.5: the improved F-V-procomplex from Lη_μD
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid ring, ξ a generator of ker θ with θ_r(ξ) = V(1) for all r (so θ_r(ξ̃) = p), and D ∈ D(A_inf(S)) a commutative algebra with H^i(D) = H^i(D/ξ) = 0 for i < 0 and a φ-linear automorphism φ_D. Assume S is p-torsion-free with compatible primitive p-power roots of unity, ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ), H^0(D) μ-torsion-free, and put 𝒲_r^n(D) = H^n(Lη_μD ⊗^L A_inf(S)/ξ̃_r) (with φ_D : Lη_μD ≃ Lη_ξ̃Lη_μD → Lη_μD). Assume (Assumption 11.4) every 𝒲_r^n(D) is p-torsion-free. Then (i) 𝒲_r^•(D) is a commutative dg algebra (x^2 = 0 for odd |x|); (ii) 𝒲_r^n(D) → 𝒲_r^n(D)_pre is injective, with image in θ̃_r(μ)^n𝒲_r^n(D)_pre (an isomorphism for n = 0); (iii) F, R, V, d of 𝒲(D)_pre restrict to 𝒲(D); (iv) these satisfy RF = FR, RV = VR, V(F(x)y) = xV(y), FV = p and FdV = d, R being a map of dg W_{r+1}(S)-algebras; (v) for an S-algebra B with compatible λ_r : W_r(B) → 𝒲_r^0(D), the Teichmüller identity holds, so 𝒲_r^•(D) is an F-V-procomplex for B/S and receives λ_r^• : W_rΩ^•_{B/S} → 𝒲_r^•(D).
items.note: R is defined on an explicit flat model of D with a φ-linear automorphism; Remark 11.6 describes it intrinsically when (Lη_μD)/ξ̃_r ≃ Lη_μ(D/ξ̃_r).

items.name: Proposition 11.8: Lη_μ of the perfectoid torus cochains is the q-de Rham complex
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). There is a natural injective quasi-isomorphism [ε]-Ω^•_{A_inf[U^{±1}]/A_inf} = η_{q−1}K_{A_inf[U^{±1}]}(γ_i − 1) → η_μD^• = η_{q−1}K_{A_inf[U^{±1/p^∞}]}(γ_i − 1), and (Lη_μD)/ξ̃_r → Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1}(D/ξ̃_r) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: The polynomial version of Lemma 9.6: for non-integral weights [ε]^k − 1 divides μ and the summand is killed by η_μ (Lemma 7.9).

items.name: Lemma 11.9: the groups 𝒲_r^n(D) for the perfectoid torus
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). For each n ≥ 0, 𝒲_r^n(D) ≅ ⊕_{a:{1,…,d}→p^{−r}Z} W_{r−u(a)}(O)^{⊕C(d,n)} as W_r(O)-modules (u(a) as in Theorem 10.12); in particular 𝒲_r^n(D) is p-torsion-free, so Assumption 11.4 holds, whereas 𝒲_r^n(D)_pre = H^n(D/ξ̃_r) has much torsion from non-integral weights.

items.name: Lemma 11.11 and Corollary 11.12: the structure maps for the torus
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). There is a unique family of W_r(O)-algebra maps λ_r : W_r(O[T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}]) → 𝒲_r^0(D) with λ_r([T_i]) = U_i commuting with F, R, V, and each λ_r is an isomorphism; hence there are unique maps λ_r^• : W_rΩ^•_{O[T^{±1}]/O} → 𝒲_r^•(D) compatible with d, F, R, V and products.

items.name: Theorem 11.7 / 11.13: the de Rham–Witt complex of the torus realized by Lη_μ
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). For all r ≥ 1 and n ≥ 0, λ_r^n : W_rΩ^n_{O[T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/O} → 𝒲_r^n(D) = H^n(Lη_μD ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_inf/ξ̃_r) is an isomorphism, compatible with d, F, R, V and products.
items.locator: Theorem 11.7, p. 349; Theorem 11.13 and proof, pp. 352–355
items.note: Proof: both sides decompose by weights a : {1, …, d} → p^{−r}Z into sums of W_{r−u(a)}(O) (Lemma 11.14), so it suffices to check after ⊗ W_r(k); there 𝒲_r^•(D)_k ≅ W_rΩ^•_{k[T^{±1}]/k} by the Cartier isomorphism (Lemma 11.16), and a dg endomorphism of W_rΩ^•_{k[T^{±1}]/k} that is the identity in degree 0 is the identity.

items.name: Lemma 11.14: isotypic decompositions and reduction to the residue field
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). For n ≥ 0, 𝒲_r^n(D) and W_rΩ^n_{O[T^{±1}]/O} admit unique decompositions ⊕_{a:{1,…,d}→p^{−r}Z} M_a on which (1/p^s)γ_i ∈ Z[1/p]^d acts on M_a by [ζ_{p^s}^{a(i)}], with each M_a a finite sum of copies of W_{r−u(a)}(O), compatibly with λ_r^n. Consequently λ_r^n is an isomorphism iff λ_r^n ⊗_{W_r(O)} W_r(k) is.

items.name: Lemma 11.16: the residue-field reduction of 𝒲_r^•(D)
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, and D = RΓ(Z^d, A_inf[U_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, U_d^{±1/p^∞}]) with γ_i : U_i^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}U_i^{1/p^r}, a commutative algebra in D(A_inf) with Frobenius φ_D (Frobenius on A_inf, U_i ↦ U_i^p). There is an isomorphism of dg algebras 𝒲_r^•(D) ⊗_{W_r(O)} W_r(k) ≅ W_rΩ^•_{k[T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/k}, compatible in degree 0 with λ_r^0 ⊗ W_r(k). (It is obtained from Lη_μD ⊗^L W(k) ≃ Ω^•_{W(k)[T^{±1}]/W(k)} — the q-de Rham complex at q = 1 — and the Cartier isomorphism H^n(Ω^•_{W_r(k)[T^{±1}]/W_r(k)}) ≅ W_rΩ^n_{k[T^{±1}]/k}.)
items.note: Uses Illusie–Raynaud's Cartier isomorphism (§III.1.5). The printed proof reverses 'Tor-independent from W_r(O) over W_r(k)' (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 11.17: junk torsion as a de Rham–Witt quotient
items.statement: Let R be small formally smooth over O with generic fibre X. For integers r ≥ 1, s ≥ 0 there are natural isomorphisms H^i(Lη_{[ζ_{p^{r+s}}]−1}RΓ_proet(X, W_r(Ô_X^+))) ≅^{φ^s} H^i(W̃_{r+s}Ω_R ⊗^L_{W_{r+s}(O)} W_r(O)) ≅ (W_{r+s}Ω^{i,cont}_{R/O}/V^rW_sΩ^{i,cont}_{R/O}){−i}, where W_{r+s}(O) → W_r(O) is the restriction. As s → ∞ the left side becomes almost isomorphic to H^i_proet(X, W_r(Ô_X^+)), which interprets the 'junk torsion' through non-integral de Rham–Witt terms.
items.locator: Proposition 11.17 and the remark after it, pp. 356–357

items.name: Lemma 12.2: elements of A_crys
items.statement: Let q = [ε] ∈ A_crys. (i) (q − 1)^{p−1}/p ∈ A_crys and is topologically nilpotent for the p-adic topology. (ii) For every n ≥ 0, (q − 1)^n/(n+1)! ∈ A_crys, tending p-adically to 0. (iii) log(q) = (q − 1)u for a unit u ∈ A_crys. Hence log(q)^n/(n!(q − 1)) = u^n(q − 1)^{n−1}/n! ∈ A_crys, tending to 0.

items.name: Lemma 12.3: A_crys(R)^□ is μ-torsion-free
items.statement: For R small with framing □, A_crys(R)^□ := A(R)^□ ⊗̂_{A_inf} A_crys is the derived p-completion of a free A_crys-module and is μ-torsion-free.
items.note: Any smooth O/p-algebra is free over O/p, being a base change from an artinian subring; T_p(⊕_I A_crys/μ) embeds in ∏_I T_p(A_crys/μ) = 0.

items.name: Lemma 12.4: the q-derivative as a Taylor series
items.statement: On A_crys(R)^□, ∂_q/∂_q log(U_i) = Σ_{n≥1} (log(q)^n/(n!(q − 1)))(∂/∂log(U_i))^n; equivalently γ_i = exp(log(q)∂/∂log(U_i)).

items.name: Corollary 12.5: the q-de Rham complex over A_crys is the de Rham complex
items.statement: For R small with framing □ there is an isomorphism of complexes q-Ω^•_{A(R)^□/A_inf} ⊗̂_{A_inf} A_crys ≅ Ω^•_{A_crys(R)^□/A_crys}, the identity in degree 0 (not an isomorphism of dg algebras); the right side computes RΓ_crys((Spec R/p)/A_crys), so AΩ_R ⊗̂^L A_crys ≃ RΓ_crys((Spec R/p)/A_crys) noncanonically.
items.locator: Corollary 12.5 and the remarks after it, pp. 360–361
items.note: ∂_q/∂_q log(U_i) = (∂/∂log(U_i))h_i with h_i an automorphism, and K_M(g_ih_i) ≅ K_M(g_i).

items.name: The all-units construction D_Σ and R_∞,Σ for very small R
items.statement: Call a small formally smooth O-algebra R very small if Spf R also admits a closed immersion into some Ĝ_m^n. For a finite set Σ ⊂ R^× with Spf R → Ĝ_m^{|Σ|} a closed immersion and containing d units giving an étale framing, let S_Σ = A_crys[x_u^{±1} : u ∈ Σ], D_Σ the p-adically completed PD envelope of S_Σ → R/p (flat over Z_p), S_∞,Σ ⊃ S_Σ adjoining all x_u^{1/p^∞}, R_∞,Σ the p-adic completion of the normalization of R in (R ⊗_{S_Σ} S_∞,Σ)[1/p] (perfectoid), and Γ = ∏_{u∈Σ} Z_p(1) acting by x_u^{1/p^r} ↦ [ε]^{1/p^r}x_u^{1/p^r}. Then x_u ↦ [u^♭] gives D_Σ → A_crys(R_∞,Σ/p) = A_inf(R_∞,Σ) ⊗̂_{A_inf} A_crys, Γ-equivariantly.
items.note: AI.4: 'the all-coordinates construction'. Filtered colimits over Σ make everything strictly functorial.

items.name: Lemma 12.6: the Lie algebra action on D_Σ
items.statement: Lie Γ ≅ ∏_{u∈Σ} Z_p(1) acts on D_Σ by g = log(γ) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1}(γ − 1)^n/n (convergent, with values in ([ε] − 1)D_Σ), and γ = exp(g); the basis vector g_u acts by log([ε])∂/∂log(x_u), the derivation ∂/∂log(x_u) extending uniquely to D_Σ.

items.name: Corollary 12.7: from crystalline cochains to η_μ of group cochains
items.statement: (i) K_{D_Σ}((∂/∂log(x_u))_{u∈Σ}) ≅ η_μK_{D_Σ}((g_u)_{u∈Σ}), the left side computing RΓ_crys(Spec(R/p)/A_crys). (ii) K_{D_Σ}((g_u)_u) ≅ K_{D_Σ}((γ_u − 1)_u), which computes RΓ_cont(Γ, D_Σ). Hence a natural map α_R^0 : K_{D_Σ}((∂/∂log(x_u))_u) → η_μK_{D_Σ}((γ_u − 1)_u) → η_μK_{A_crys(R_∞,Σ/p)}((γ_u − 1)_u). The commutative dga K_{D_Σ}((g_u)_u) models the E_∞-algebra RΓ_cont(Γ, D_Σ).
items.locator: Corollary 12.7 and the remarks after it, pp. 363–364
items.note: The printed proof writes g_u = log(μ)∂/∂log(x_u) and log(μ) = μv for log([ε]) (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 12.8: the subrings A_crys^(m) and η_μ
items.statement: Let A_crys^(m) ⊂ A_crys be the p-adic completion of the A_inf-subalgebra generated by ξ^j/j!, j ≤ m. (i) For m ≥ p^2, ξ̃_r = p^rv for a unit v ∈ A_crys^(m) and Lemma 12.2 holds in A_crys^(m). (ii) The ideals {x : μx ∈ p^rA_crys^(m)} and p^rA_crys^(m) are intertwined. (iii) ∩_r (μ/φ^{−r}(μ))A_crys^(m) = μA_crys^(m). (iv) For m ≥ p^2, (η_μK_{A_inf(R_∞,Σ)}((γ_u − 1)_u)) ⊗̂^L A_crys^(m) → η_μK_{A_inf(R_∞,Σ) ⊗̂ A_crys^(m)}((γ_u − 1)_u) is a quasi-isomorphism, the left side computing AΩ_R ⊗̂^L A_crys^(m). (v) α_R^0 factors canonically through α_R : K_{D_Σ}((∂/∂log(x_u))_u) → (colim_m η_μK_{A_inf(R_∞,Σ) ⊗̂ A_crys^(m)}((γ_u − 1)_u))^∧_p, whose target computes AΩ_R ⊗̂^L A_crys.
items.note: A_crys/μ is not p-adically separated, which is why A_crys^(m) is used; (ii)–(iii) are proved over the noetherian Z_p[[T]] (T ↦ [ε]^{1/p}) and base changed.

items.name: Proposition 12.9: α_R is a quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: For R very small and Σ as above, α_R : K_{D_Σ}((∂/∂log(x_u))_{u∈Σ}) → (colim_m η_μK_{A_inf(R_∞,Σ) ⊗̂_{A_inf} A_crys^(m)}((γ_u − 1)_u))^∧_p is a quasi-isomorphism. Passing to the filtered colimit over Σ, these maps are strictly functorial in R and globalize to Theorem 12.1.
items.note: Proof: a unique lift Spf D_Σ → Spf A_crys(R)^□ reduces to the framed case, where Corollary 12.5 applies.

items.name: Lemma 13.4: rigid geometry over B_dR^+/ξ^n
items.statement: Let C be algebraically closed complete over Q_p and R a complete Tate B_dR^+/ξ^n-algebra. (i) There is a surjection B_dR^+/ξ^n⟨X_1, …, X_m⟩ → R iff R/ξ is topologically of finite type over C ('R is topologically of finite type'). (ii) Such R is noetherian and every ideal of R is closed. (iii) A p-adically complete p-torsion-free A_inf/ξ^n-algebra R_0 that is a quotient of A_inf/ξ^n⟨X_1, …, X_m⟩ is coherent, every ideal I with R_0/I p-torsion-free is finitely generated, and R_0[1/p] is topologically of finite type. (iv) Every R topologically of finite type over B_dR^+/ξ^n has a ring of definition topologically of finite type over A_inf/ξ^n.

items.name: Very small smooth affinoids and the thickenings D_Σ(R)
items.statement: A smooth Tate C-algebra R of dimension d is very small if there are finite sets {T_1, …, T_d} ⊂ Σ ⊂ (R°)^× such that C⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Σ}⟩ → R, X_u ↦ u, is surjective and Spa(R, R°) → T^d given by the T_i is étale and a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps (Σ may be enlarged). With B_dR^+⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Σ}⟩ := lim_r B_dR^+/ξ^r⟨(X_u^{±1})⟩, D_Σ(R) is its completion along I(R) = ker(→ R); all powers I(R)^n are closed, so D_Σ(R) is a complete separated B_dR^+-algebra, and the derivations ∂/∂log(X_v) = X_v∂/∂X_v extend continuously to D_Σ(R). Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+} := K_{D_Σ(R)}((∂/∂log(X_u))_{u∈Σ}).
items.locator: Definition 13.5 and Construction 13.6, pp. 371–372; the paragraph before Lemma 13.13, p. 379
items.note: CP.3: 'construct the canonical B_dR^+-valued deformation of de Rham cohomology by the infinitesimal/PD-style embedding system of BMS1 §13, with the completed tensor and coordinate-independence proof'.

items.name: Lemma 13.7: noetherian approximation of very small affinoids
items.statement: Let R be a very small smooth Tate C-algebra with {T_1, …, T_d} ⊂ Σ. After enlarging Σ there are: a smooth affinoid S = Spa(A, A°) of finite type over W(k')[1/p] for a perfect field k' ⊂ k (one may take k' = F_p) with a W(k')-algebra map A → C; a smooth Spa(R_A, R_A°) → Spa(A, A°) with R ≅ R_A ⊗̂_A C; and {T_1, …, T_d} ⊂ Σ_A ⊂ (R_A°)^× mapping into Σ (fixing the T_i) such that A⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Σ_A}⟩ → R_A is surjective and Spa(R_A, R_A°) → T^d_S is étale and a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps.
items.note: Uses de Jong's alterations to write O as a filtered colimit of regular finite type Z_p-algebras, and Lemmas 13.8–13.10.

items.name: Lemma 13.8: small perturbations preserve surjectivity
items.statement: Let f : M → N be a map of p-torsion-free p-adically complete abelian groups with f[1/p] surjective. There is m ≥ 0 such that every g : M → N with g ≡ f mod p^m has g[1/p] surjective.

items.name: Lemma 13.9: surjectivity spreads out from a rank-one point
items.statement: Let A → B →^α C be maps of affinoid algebras topologically of finite type over a nonarchimedean field K, and x ∈ Spa(A, A°) a rank-one point with B ⊗̂_A k(x) → C ⊗̂_A k(x) surjective. Then there is a rational subset U ∋ x with B ⊗̂_A A_U → C ⊗̂_A A_U surjective. (For x of rank > 1 this fails: take C = A_V for a rational V containing the rank-one generalization of x but not x.)
items.locator: Lemma 13.9 and the remark after it, pp. 374–376

items.name: Lemma 13.10: an integrality criterion for rings of definition
items.statement: Let B_0 ⊂ C_0 be p-adically complete p-torsion-free rings with C_0 topologically generated over B_0 by f_1, …, f_r such that each f_i ∈ B_0[1/p] and there are monic P_i ∈ B_0[x] with P_i(f_i) ∈ pC_0. Then p^kC_0 ⊂ B_0 for some k.

items.name: Lemma 13.11: the B_dR^+-lift R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 13.7, fix a continuous lift A → B_dR^+ of A → C (it exists as A is smooth over a discretely valued field). Then R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+ := lim_n R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+/ξ^n is a ξ-adically complete flat B_dR^+-algebra with (R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+)/ξ^n = R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+/ξ^n topologically free over B_dR^+/ξ^n and (R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+)/ξ = R.
items.note: Uses Huber's Corollary 1.7.3(iii) and Raynaud–Gruson's freeness criterion (Théorème 3.3.5) for the p-torsion-free quotient.

items.name: Lemma 13.12: explicit description of D_Σ(R)
items.statement: (i) There is a unique topological isomorphism D_{Σ_A}(R_A) ≅ R_A[[(X_u − u)_{u∈Σ_A, u≠T_1,…,T_d}]] compatible with the projections to R_A and the A⟨(X_u^{±1})⟩-algebra structures (X_{T_i} ↦ T_i). (ii) If Σ is sufficiently large, D_Σ(R) ≅ (R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+)[[(X_u − ũ)_{u∈Σ, u≠T_1,…,T_d}]] compatibly with the projection to R and the B_dR^+⟨(X_u^{±1})⟩-algebra structures, for lifts ũ of u. In particular D_Σ(R) is ξ-adically complete and ξ-torsion-free.

items.name: Lemma 13.13: crystalline and de Rham complexes of D_Σ(R) agree
items.statement: Let D̃_Σ(R) be the completion of (D_Σ(R)/ξ) ⊗̂_C R → R and D̃_Σ(R_A) that of D_Σ(R) ⊗̂_{B_dR^+} (R_A ⊗̂_A B_dR^+) → R. The maps Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+}/ξ → Ω^•_{D̃_Σ(R)/C} ← Ω^•_{R/C} and Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+} → Ω^•_{D̃_Σ(R_A)/B_dR^+} ← Ω^•_{R_A/A} ⊗̂_A B_dR^+ are quasi-isomorphisms. In particular Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+} → Ω^•_{D_{Σ'}(R)/B_dR^+} is a quasi-isomorphism for Σ ⊂ Σ' sufficiently large.

items.name: B_dR^+-cohomology of very small affinoids and of proper smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: For a very small smooth Tate C-algebra R and X = Spa(R, R°), C^•_crys(X/B_dR^+) := colim_Σ Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR^+} over sufficiently large finite Σ ⊂ (R°)^×, a presheaf of B_dR^+-complexes on very small smooth affinoids with RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊗^L_{B_dR^+} C ≃ Ω^•_{R/C}. For a proper smooth adic space X/C, RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+) ∈ D(B_dR^+) is the hypercohomology of U ↦ C^•_crys(U/B_dR^+) on very small open affinoids; RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+) ⊗^L C ≅ RΓ_dR(X), so it is a perfect B_dR^+-complex (derived ξ-complete with finite-dimensional reduction).
items.locator: Definition 13.14 and the paragraph after it, p. 381; §13.3, Definition 13.18 and the paragraph after it, p. 384

items.name: Proposition 13.15: formal schemes over O are pulled back from complete noetherian local W-algebras
items.statement: Let (W, 𝔪) be a complete noetherian local ring with residue field k and O an 𝔪-adically complete local W-algebra with O/𝔪O 0-dimensional with residue field k. For every proper flat adic formal scheme 𝔛_O over O (with the 𝔪-adic topology) there are a complete noetherian local W-algebra R with residue field k, a proper flat adic formal scheme 𝔛_R over R, a W-algebra map η : R → O and an isomorphism η^*𝔛_R ≅ 𝔛_O.
items.note: 𝔛_R is a versal deformation of the special fibre (Schlessinger); formal smoothness of h_R → Def extends to ind-artinian rings such as O/𝔪^nO. The printed proof refers to parts '(i) and (ii)' and a part '(iii)' of a two-part statement (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Corollary 13.16 (Conrad–Gabber): spreading out proper rigid spaces
items.statement: Let C/K be an extension of complete nonarchimedean fields with the same residue field. Every proper rigid space X/C is the fibre over a point η ∈ S(C) of a proper flat morphism f : 𝒳 → S of rigid spaces over K; if X is smooth, S, 𝒳 and f can be taken smooth. In particular every proper smooth rigid space over C is a fibre of a proper smooth morphism of smooth rigid spaces over a discretely valued subfield of C.
items.note: BMS1 prove this special case themselves from Proposition 13.15 (formal models, with Lütkebohmert's properness), since Conrad–Gabber's stronger result, allowing arbitrary residue fields, was in preparation. It is the input to Theorems 13.3 and 13.19.

items.name: Remark 13.20: B_dR^+-cohomology in the discretely valued case
items.statement: If X = X_0 ⊗̂_K C for a proper smooth adic space X_0 over a discretely valued subfield K ⊂ C, there is a canonical identification H^i_dR(X_0/K) ⊗_K B_dR^+ ≅ H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+), using the unique continuous lift K → B_dR^+ of K → C.
items.note: CP.3: 'When X descends to a proper smooth X_0/K, compare that deformation with H_dR(X_0/K) ⊗_K B_dR^+'.

items.name: Proposition 13.21: crystalline cohomology over A_crys after inverting p (Berthelot–Ogus)
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be a proper smooth formal scheme over O_C, Y = 𝔛 ×_{Spf O} Spec O/p and Ȳ its special fibre. For a section k → O/p there is a canonical φ-equivariant isomorphism H^i_crys(Y/A_crys)[1/p] ≅ H^i_crys(Ȳ/W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} A_crys[1/p]; in particular H^i_crys(Y/A_crys)[1/p] is finite free over A_crys[1/p]. If k = F̄_p the section is unique.
items.note: CP.2: 'Prove the relevant crystalline change-of-base/invariance statement after p-inversion'. A variant of Berthelot–Ogus (Invent. Math. 72, 1983); proof by Frobenius being an isomorphism after inverting p and Y ≅ Ȳ ×_k O/p^{1/p^n} for n ≫ 0.

items.name: Proposition 13.23: B_dR^+-cohomology in the good reduction case
items.statement: For 𝔛 proper smooth over O_C with generic fibre X and Y = 𝔛_{O/p}, there is a natural quasi-isomorphism RΓ_crys(Y/A_crys) ⊗_{A_crys} B_dR^+ ≅ RΓ_crys(X/B_dR^+); hence H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+) ≅ H^i_crys(Y/A_crys) ⊗_{A_crys} B_dR^+ is free.
items.note: Both sides are computed by the explicit embedding complexes of §§12.2 and 13.1.
